        case 'signup':
          return { create: { attributes: { customerId: key } } };
        case 'suspend':
          return { key, signal: 'suspend', payload: {} };
        case 'reinstate':
          return { key, signal: 'reinstate', payload: {} };
        case 'churn':
          return { key, signal: 'churn', payload: {} };
      }
    }),
  ])
  .store(sqlite.store(Tenancy, 'tenancies.db'))
  .runner(shell)
  .handler(tenancyReviewFlow, { states: { reviewed: Current, failed: Current } })
  .signals({
    monthlyReview: H.move(ReviewDue).from([Current]),
    suspend: H.move(Suspended).from([Current, ReviewDue]),
    reinstate: H.move(Current).from([Suspended]),
    churn: H.move(Churned).from([Current, ReviewDue, Suspended]),
  });

const OurTurn = H.state('our turn', 'pending');
const AwaitingVendor = H.state('awaiting vendor', 'active');
const Agreed = H.state('agreed', 'succeeded');
const WeWalkedAway = H.state('we walked away', 'concluded');
const TheyWalkedAway = H.state('they walked away', 'concluded');
const Expired = H.state('expired', 'concluded');
const NegotiationFailed = H.state('negotiation failed', 'failed');

const Negotiation = H.work('Negotiation')
  .attributes({ vendor: z.string(), expiresAt: z.number() })
  .fields({ item: z.string(), targetPriceUsd: z.number() })
  .states([OurTurn, AwaitingVendor, Agreed, WeWalkedAway, TheyWalkedAway, Expired, NegotiationFailed])
  .signals({ vendorOffered: { offer: z.string() }, vendorWalkedAway: { reason: z.string() } })
  .timers(t => ({ expiry: t.attribute('expiresAt') }))
  .key(unit => `${unit.attributes.vendor}/${unit.fields.item}`);

const negotiatorRole = H.role('negotiator')
  .intents(['read'])
  .instructions('Decide the next move in the procurement negotiation and write the message to the vendor.')
  .input({ vendor: z.string(), item: z.string(), targetPriceUsd: z.number(), vendorOffer: z.string() })
  .output({ move: z.enum(['counter', 'accept', 'walkAway']), message: z.string() });
const negotiator = H.agent('negotiator', negotiatorRole).model(opus).pool(apiAccount);

const sendToVendor = H.command('send-to-vendor', ['procurement/send']);
const vendorOfferPayload = z.object({ offer: z.string() });

const negotiationRoundFlow = H.flow('negotiation-round')
  .requires({ vendor: z.string(), item: z.string(), targetPriceUsd: z.number() })
  .step('offer', negotiator, c => {
    const offers = c.signals
      .filter(signal => signal.name === 'vendorOffered')
      .flatMap(signal => {
        const parsed = vendorOfferPayload.safeParse(signal.payload);
        return parsed.success ? [parsed.data.offer] : [];
      });
    return {
      vendor: c.input.vendor,
      item: c.input.item,
      targetPriceUsd: c.input.targetPriceUsd,
      vendorOffer: offers.length > 0 ? offers[offers.length - 1] : 'no offer yet',
    };
  })
  .step('send', sendToVendor, c => ({ args: [c.input.vendor], stdin: c.out.offer.message }), {
    retry: H.retry.exponential({ maxRetries: 3, initialDelayMs: 30_000 }),
  })
  .ends(['awaitingVendor', 'agreed', 'walkedAway'], c =>
    c.out.offer.move === 'accept' ? 'agreed' : c.out.offer.move === 'walkAway' ? 'walkedAway' : 'awaitingVendor',
  );

const vendorReply = z.object({ negotiation: z.string(), walkAway: z.boolean(), message: z.string() });

const negotiationLane = H.lane('negotiations', Negotiation)
  .supply([
    H.supply.operator(),
    http.webhook(Negotiation, { path: '/vendor-replies', port: H.slot.port(1), secret: H.env('VENDOR_WEBHOOK_SECRET') }, body => {
      const parsed = vendorReply.safeParse(body);
      if (!parsed.success) return null;
      return parsed.data.walkAway
        ? { key: parsed.data.negotiation, signal: 'vendorWalkedAway', payload: { reason: parsed.data.message } }
        : { key: parsed.data.negotiation, signal: 'vendorOffered', payload: { offer: parsed.data.message } };
    }),
  ])
  .store(sqlite.store(Negotiation, 'negotiations.db'))
  .runner(shell)
  .handler(negotiationRoundFlow, {
    states: {
      awaitingVendor: AwaitingVendor,
      agreed: Agreed,
      walkedAway: WeWalkedAway,
      failed: NegotiationFailed,
    },
  })
  .signals({
    vendorOffered: H.move(OurTurn).from([AwaitingVendor]),
    vendorWalkedAway: H.move(TheyWalkedAway).from([OurTurn, AwaitingVendor]),
    expiry: H.move(Expired).from([OurTurn, AwaitingVendor]),
  });

const lifecycleOrder = H.policy.schedule('lifecycle-order', c => {
  const inconclusive = c.metrics.outcomes({ lane: experimentLane, windowDays: 365 }).share(Inconclusive);
  const experimentsOftenInconclusive = inconclusive.n >= 10 && inconclusive.rate !== null && inconclusive.rate > 0.5;
  const deferred = (candidate: { is: (typeof c.candidates)[number]['is'] }): number =>
    Number(experimentsOftenInconclusive && candidate.is(experimentLane));
  return { start: [...c.candidates].sort((a, b) => deferred(a) - deferred(b)) };
});

const ownerAccess = H.access('owner').allows([
  H.ops.readWork,
  H.ops.createWork,
  H.ops.signalWork,
  H.ops.resolveBlocks,
  H.ops.readTelemetry,
]);

export const lifecycles = H.harness('hostile-lifecycles')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('lifecycles-ledger.db'))
  .lanes([experimentLane, tenancyLane, negotiationLane])
  .schedule(lifecycleOrder)
  .clients([claudeCode.supervisor('owner-supervisor', ownerAccess, { port: H.slot.port(2) })])
  .projections([markdown.board('BOARD.md'), markdown.telemetry('TELEMETRY.md')]);

=== END ===

# You are designing harness-dsl, a TypeScript DSL for stateful agentic-work harnesses.

# harness-dsl design principles

These are the owner's decisions. A variant that violates one is worse, however elegant. A variant may propose changing one only by stating the principle it breaks and why, in its design notes.

## Vision

1. **Stateless LLMs, stateful harness.** Every model call is a pure function. All state lives in the harness. The harness gets better over time not because models learn but because it feeds the right memory to the right call.
2. **The harness is about work.** Units of work, kinds of work (Bug, Feature, Epic, ServiceHeartbeat, Exercise), hierarchies of kinds, lifecycles, where work comes from, where its state lives, what runs next. The framework is honest about this. It does not hide behind "general purpose".
3. **An LLM is a component, not a requirement.** A harness with zero model calls is a first-class harness. Deterministic scripts and model calls compose through the same executable interface.
4. **Intelligence lives in determinism.** Policies (what to pick, what to recall, what to schedule) are deterministic functions, authored once, reading harness state and metrics at decision time. Policies never change themselves. The harness changes behaviour because policies read changed state.

## Dividing line

5. **Opinionated about shape, agnostic about backend.** The kernel defines what a work unit, a lifecycle, a memory item, a policy, a ledger entry *is*. It never cares where any of them is stored, which vendor serves a model, or which tool the operator uses. Like Eloquent: strict about how you model, indifferent to which database.
6. **Defaults ship, and pass the delete test.** First-party backends ship in the box (SQLite ledger, JSONL memory store, Claude Code driver, folder supplier). Each is one implementation of a public interface. Delete any of them and the kernel still compiles and runs.
7. **`H.*` is kernel vocabulary only.** Shapes and builders. Anything with a backend lives in a subpath (`harness-dsl/claude-code`, `harness-dsl/sqlite`, `harness-dsl/linear`), whether first-party or not. No vendor, CLI, file format or product name appears in `H.*`.
8. **Three sorts of entity.** *Kinds* are pure vocabulary and carry no backend (work kind, state, memory kind, role). *Instances* are specific resources and carry their backend (account, model, runner). *Pivots* connect kinds and instances per harness (pool = accounts × policy, agent = role × model, lane = work kind × suppliers × store × handler, journal = memory kind × store × recall).
9. **Every pivot has a noun.** A pivot enters the DSL only when we can name what it produces. `bind`, `wire`, `attach`, `connect` are not nouns; they are the absence of a concept.
10. **Relationships do not live on kinds.** A work kind does not know who supplies it, stores it or handles it. A role does not know which model runs it. Putting a relationship on a kind makes the kind less reusable.

## Mechanics

11. **Descriptors are immutable and stateless.** Every builder method returns a new descriptor. Nothing is read from the environment at definition time; `H.env('NAME')` and `H.slot.port(n)` are references the runtime resolves. Derived descriptors must be renamed; the runtime refuses two descriptors with one name.
12. **Lifecycle skeleton.** An attempt has one of three outcomes: succeeded, failed, cancelled. This is the harness's track record, and metrics on models, agents, runners and accounts are computed from it. A unit is at one of four positions: pending, active, waiting (parked, holding no capacity, not schedulable), terminal. The scheduler and the board are defined on positions. A kind's named states are entities (shareable); each declares its position, and each terminal state declares its verdict for the kind's own outcome rate: success, failure or neutral, with no default. Blocked (waiting on a human) is an attempt state, not a unit state. A unit outlives its attempts; an attempt's failure moves the unit only where the kind says so. (Amended 2026-11-01 after generation 0: eight of eight variants broke the five-outcome form, and the adversaries showed why.)
13. **Triggers are relationships.** A trigger connects a source (a transition, later also time, external events, metric thresholds) to a consequence (create work in a lane, run an executable, record memory). Flows stay blind to other kinds. Triggers fire only from recorded ledger events and their firings are recorded.
14. **Memory is forward-phrased and atomic.** "Do X when Y because Z", never history. The kernel owns the envelope (id, created, `when`: the kinds, roles, skills and resources an item applies to). Recall is a deterministic policy over items and scope, ranked by specificity and by track record (items present in succeeded attempts rise). Experience (can be wrong, stale, deduped) and taste (the owner's preference, never wrong, broadly scoped) are different kinds.
15. **The ledger is the kernel's only state.** Runs, attempts, invocations, transitions, the pending queue, quota. Its backend is pluggable. There is no kernel work store: domain state lives where the owner's adapter puts it, and a unit may have no store at all.
16. **Supply, store and scheduling are three pillars.** Suppliers produce units (folder, poll, webhook, schedule, operator). Stores hold unit state (one adapter may be both). The scheduler decides what runs next from pending units, lane WIP limits, capacity (runner slots, account eligibility) and a policy. Without a scheduler there is a library, not a harness.
17. **Human-in-the-loop is kernel.** Halting an attempt for an outside decision is universal. Who resolves it, through which surface, is not: the supervisor is one optional client of a control API made of operations, and operations (not capability strings) are what a client is granted.
18. **Metrics are queryable and honest.** Computed from ledger transitions, with sample counts beside every rate, so policy authors write exploration deliberately. Success is defined by the kind's terminal states, never by "the flow finished".

## Ergonomics standards

19. A first-time reader predicts what each line does from its name. Builders chain. Names are nouns for things and verbs for settings. Units sit in names or types (`budgetTokens`, `maxUsd`), never implied.
20. Full inference. Scenario code needs no `as`, `any`, `!` or `@ts-ignore`. A `.d.ts` that uses `any` to make inference "work" fails this standard.
21. Small surface. The fewest entities and methods that express the whole scenario battery without escape hatches. An entity with one use is suspect. A method nobody in the battery calls is removed.
22. No two words for one thing. Run, attempt, invocation, step have one definition each, or fewer words.


# Scenario battery

# Scenario 1: coding team

A product team's harness, the shape harness-dsl was first built for.

## Must express

- Three kinds of work in a hierarchy: Epic decomposes into Features; Bugs arrive on their own. Epic completes when its Features do. Feature and Bug share most of their lifecycle and handler but differ in how many build-and-audit rounds they get (Bug 3, Feature 5).
- Supply from three places at once for Bugs: an issue tracker (Linear), a folder of markdown files, and the operator typing to the supervisor. Features from the tracker and the operator. Epics from the tracker only.
- Bug and Feature state is kept in the tracker; the harness is not the source of truth for them.
- A builder agent on a worktree per attempt, with a file-lease guard (two attempts may not write the same file) and a stop check that runs the project's checks before the agent may stop.
- An auditor agent that finds deficits; the loop continues until none remain or rounds run out. The builder may halt the attempt for an owner decision.
- Accounts: three Claude subscriptions in a pool with per-account quota shares, drained soonest-expiring first, falling back to an API account. Model choice for the builder reads the ledger: use the cheaper model until its success rate on this kind of work, over 14 days and at least 20 samples, drops below 0.85.
- Memory: experience ("when touching payments, run the ledger fixture first, because the migration reorders rows") recalled by builder and auditor, recorded by the auditor; taste ("prefer early returns over nested conditionals") recalled by builder and planner, written by the owner.
- A service heartbeat every five minutes, all deterministic, whose failure creates a Bug through a trigger. The heartbeat flow must not reference the Bug kind.
- Scheduler: heartbeats first, then bugs, features, epics; a WIP limit of 2 concurrent bugs and 1 epic; starvation protection for features.
- Supervisor: a Claude Code session granted read and write on work, blocker resolution, memory writes, telemetry and account shares, plus one custom operation (a production health probe).
- Board and telemetry projections written as Markdown files.

## Hostile aspects

- The heartbeat kind must have no store and must still appear in telemetry.
- The same handler flow serves two kinds with different round counts without duplication.
- The model-choice policy must expose sample counts; a variant that hides them fails.


---

# Scenario 2: support triage

Customer conversations arrive from a helpdesk webhook. Nothing here touches files.

## Must express

- One kind of work, Conversation, supplied by a webhook (push) and by a periodic poll of the helpdesk for anything the webhook missed. State lives in the helpdesk via its API; the harness holds nothing but its ledger.
- Lifecycle: new, classifying, drafting, awaiting approval, sent, closed by customer, escalated. A human approves every outgoing reply (halt), except for a category the policy marks safe after 200 approved samples with zero rejections.
- Two agents: a classifier on a cheap model, a drafter on a stronger one. The drafter recalls taste (tone, phrases to avoid) and experience ("when the customer mentions a refund older than 30 days, cite policy 4.2"). A reviewer role (human, through the supervisor) records taste from its edits.
- Deadlines: each conversation carries an SLA; the scheduler orders by time to breach, not by arrival. A breached SLA fires a trigger that escalates (creates an Escalation unit in another lane with its own handler and a human-only flow).
- External cancellation: if the customer replies while a draft is awaiting approval, the attempt is cancelled and the unit returns to classifying with the new message.
- Per-unit cost ceiling: no conversation may spend more than $0.40 of model cost; a unit that would exceed it halts for a human.
- Metrics the policy reads: approval rate by category and by model, with sample counts.

## Hostile aspects

- Cancellation from outside an active attempt.
- A trigger whose source is time (SLA breach), not a transition.
- A cost ceiling scoped to a unit, not an account.
- A lane whose handler contains no model call at all (Escalation).


---

# Scenario 3: research pipeline

A team runs literature-style research: a topic goes in, a sourced report comes out.

## Must express

- Kind Topic, supplied by the operator and by a weekly schedule that re-opens topics tagged "recurring". Topics are stored in the harness's own store (no external system), so the first-party store is the right choice here.
- Handler: fan out 20 search-and-extract calls as one cloud batch on a cheap model (the batch API discount matters), gather, then one synthesis call on a strong model, then a deterministic citation check command that fails the attempt if a citation does not resolve.
- Memory with a vector-store backend: prior report findings are a memory kind recalled by the synthesizer by semantic similarity. Recall is still a deterministic policy; the vector store is a backend. Experience about sources ("when the source is a preprint server, downgrade confidence") is a second kind in a JSONL store.
- Per-topic cost ceiling of $3; the scheduler never starts a topic whose projected cost (from the metric: mean cost of succeeded attempts of this kind) would pass the remaining daily budget of $40.
- Outcome: a report is delivered, or the topic is parked (not enough sources), or it is cancelled by the operator. Parked is not failure.
- The synthesizer's model is chosen by a policy that compares two strong models on a metric the owner defines: citation-check pass rate.

## Hostile aspects

- A memory backend that is not a file and a recall policy that uses similarity, while recall stays deterministic.
- A cloud batch step inside a flow, priced at the batch discount in telemetry.
- Budget as a scheduling input (daily, across units).
- A terminal outcome, parked, that is neither success nor failure.


---

# Scenario 4: operations, no model anywhere

A platform team uses the harness purely as a durable scheduler of deterministic work. There is no model, no account, no agent in this harness. If a variant needs any of them to compile or start, it fails the scenario.

## Must express

- Kinds: Heartbeat (every 5 minutes per service), Backup (nightly per database), CertificateRenewal (weekly check, act when under 14 days), Incident (created by triggers, handled by a runbook flow that pages a human and waits).
- Suppliers: schedules only, plus the operator creating Incidents by hand through the control API over plain HTTP (no Claude Code, no MCP).
- Runners: local for heartbeats; SSH to two hosts for backups and renewals, with per-host concurrency of 1 and a disk-space preflight.
- Triggers: three consecutive failed heartbeats of one service create an Incident (a trigger over a pattern of transitions, not a single transition). A failed Backup creates an Incident at once. A Backup that succeeded but took over 2 hours records a note in a journal of operational experience, which is also a memory kind, even though nothing here reads memory into a prompt; the supervisor reads it.
- The Incident flow halts for a human acknowledgement, then runs a runbook command, then halts for a human to confirm resolution.
- Scheduler: Incidents preempt everything; a running Backup is not interrupted, but no new Backup starts while an Incident is active.
- Observers: a Slack notification on every Incident transition, and the board file.

## Hostile aspects

- Zero model calls: every executable is a command.
- A trigger whose source is a pattern across several transitions.
- Preemption rules in the scheduler.
- A control API client that is plain HTTP.
- A memory kind with no agent reading it.


---

# Scenario 5: data job with approval

A nightly data job with one human gate in the middle and a retry policy.

## Must express

- Kind NightlyLoad, supplied by a schedule at 02:00, one unit per source system (four). State in the harness's store.
- Handler: extract (command, SSH runner), validate (command), then a model call that writes a plain-language summary of anomalies, then halt for a human to approve the load, then load (command), then verify (command).
- Retry: extract and load retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff on failure, as a policy on the step, not hand-written in the command. A validation failure does not retry; it halts for a human with the validation report.
- Outcome: loaded, loaded with warnings (verify found tolerable drift), rejected by the approver, or failed. Loaded with warnings is a success for scheduling purposes but must be distinguishable in metrics and on the board.
- A unit left waiting for approval past 09:00 is cancelled by a time trigger and a new one is not created until the next night.
- Resumability: if the harness process restarts while a unit is blocked on approval, the unit is still blocked after restart and resumes at the same step when approved.
- The approver works through the supervisor; the summary agent recalls taste about what the approver wants emphasised.

## Hostile aspects

- Retry with backoff as a declared policy on a step.
- Restart survival of a blocked attempt.
- A success-with-warnings outcome that is success to the scheduler and distinct to metrics.
- A time trigger that cancels, scoped to one kind.


---

# Scenario 6: content review driven by taste

A publication runs drafts through review. The point of this harness is that it learns the owner's taste.

## Must express

- Kind Draft, supplied from a CMS by poll, state in the CMS.
- Handler: two reviewer agents on two different models each produce a critique; a deterministic command merges them; the editor (human, supervisor) accepts or returns the draft with notes.
- Taste memory grows from the editor's notes: every returned draft's notes become candidate taste items through a trigger (returned → record taste candidate), curated by the editor later through the control API (accept, merge, drop). Reviewers recall taste; taste applies to all drafts, with a smaller set scoped to a section (`sports`, `opinion`).
- A/B on models: the two reviewers' models are chosen by a policy that reads which reviewer's critiques the editor acted on more (a metric the owner defines from editor actions recorded as transitions), with sample counts, and swaps the weaker model after 50 samples.
- Experience memory also exists (fact-checking lessons), recalled by both reviewers, recorded by the fact-check command when it finds a repeat mistake.
- No worktrees, no files, no code.

## Hostile aspects

- Memory capture as a trigger consequence, not an agent tool.
- Curation operations on memory (merge, drop) exposed to the supervisor.
- A metric defined by the owner from recorded operator actions, not from attempt outcomes.
- Two agents of the same role on different models in one flow.


---

# Scenario 7: two projects, shared subscriptions

The owner runs two independent product harnesses (two repositories, two ledgers, two supervisors) that share the same three Claude subscription accounts.

## Must express

- Each harness declares the same three accounts. Account quota state (utilization windows, cooldowns) is shared between the two harnesses: if harness A drives an account into cooldown, harness B sees it. Project share caps are per harness: A may use 60% of an account's window, B 30%.
- Each harness has its own ledger (runs, attempts, telemetry) in its own SQLite file. Neither can see the other's runs.
- Fair scheduling across tenants is not the kernel's job (they are separate processes), but each scheduler must respect account eligibility that the other may have changed a second ago.
- Harness A is the coding team of scenario 1. Harness B is a documentation harness: kind DocPage, supplied from a folder, handled by a writer agent and a link-check command, stored in the folder's frontmatter.
- A shared taste journal: both harnesses recall the owner's taste from one JSONL file; each has its own experience journal.
- The owner's one supervisor session can be pointed at either harness (two control API endpoints) and sees the shared account state from both.

## Hostile aspects

- Account state that outlives and spans harnesses: where does it live, and is that a second kernel store or a backend of the ledger?
- Two ledgers, one memory store, three shared accounts: the design must say which entity owns which state without new ad-hoc concepts.
- The same entity definitions (accounts, taste journal) imported by two harness files from a shared module.


---

# Scenario 8: lifecycles that do not fit

Three kinds of work chosen to break a pending/active/succeeded/failed/cancelled skeleton. A variant must express them without lying: mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean is a failure of this scenario.

## Must express

- **Experiment**: an A/B test unit runs for two weeks, collecting a metric from a command every hour. It ends in one of: A wins, B wins, inconclusive. None of these is failure. The scheduler must treat all three as terminal; metrics must distinguish them; a policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how often are experiments inconclusive?"
- **Tenancy**: a customer's tenancy is a unit of work that is never terminal while the customer is a customer. It is re-evaluated monthly (usage review, a model-written summary, a human decision to upsell or not) and may be suspended and reinstated any number of times. It ends only on churn, which is neither success nor failure. The scheduler must not consider an active tenancy as occupying capacity between evaluations.
- **Negotiation**: a procurement negotiation unit alternates between the harness (an agent drafts the next offer) and the outside world (the vendor replies, via a webhook supplier that updates an existing unit rather than creating one). It may end in agreement, walk-away by us (a decision, not a failure), walk-away by them, or expiry (a time trigger). Each attempt is one round; the unit outlives many attempts.

## Hostile aspects

- Terminal states that are neither success nor failure, needed by metrics.
- A unit that is active for years and must not hold capacity.
- A supplier that updates an existing unit instead of creating one.
- An attempt-per-round model where the unit's identity spans attempts and external replies.
- If the variant changes the skeleton (adds outcomes, replaces the five with something else), its design notes must say what success rate means afterwards.


---

# Scenario 9: a harness watching itself

The support harness of scenario 2 observes its own metrics and acts on them. Nothing here is new work from outside; every unit created here is created by the harness about itself.

## Must express

- A trigger whose source is a metric threshold: when the approval rate for a category over the last 7 days falls below 0.9 with at least 50 samples, the harness creates one Audit unit for that category in an `audits` lane with a human-only handler. While an Audit for that category is open, no second one is created, however many samples cross the threshold.
- The same crossing records a candidate experience item scoped to the drafter role and the category: "when drafting for {category}, recall the stricter phrasing, because approvals fell to {rate}".
- When the category's rate recovers above 0.95, the open Audit is cancelled. Below 0.9 and above 0.95 are two thresholds on purpose: the trigger fires on a crossing, once, not on every sample.
- A trigger that pauses the `conversations` lane when the harness's own model error rate over the last hour exceeds 0.2 with at least 20 invocations, and resumes it when the rate falls below 0.05. Paused means: nothing new starts in the lane, running attempts finish. Both the pause and the resume are recorded on the ledger and visible on the board, with the metric value that caused them.
- Each conversation's SLA can be extended by the reviewer through the supervisor. The breach timer moves with the new deadline; the old deadline never fires.
- A policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how many Audits were opened per category this month" and "how long was the lane paused in total".

## Hostile aspects

- A trigger source that is a metric, not a transition, a time or an external event; it still fires only from recorded ledger state and its firings are recorded.
- Hysteresis: two thresholds, one firing per crossing.
- Deduplication by a group key (the category), not by kind.
- A consequence that acts on a lane, not on a unit, and is itself a recorded, queryable fact.
- A timer whose deadline changes after it was armed.


---

# Scenario 10: the power goes off

A release harness is killed mid-attempt (power cut, OOM, `kill -9`, laptop closed) and started again. This scenario states what must be true after the restart. It does not say how; a variant that satisfies every line by any mechanism passes, and its design.md must name the mechanism and what the harness author had to write for it.

## Must express

- Kind Release, supplied by the operator. Its flow, in order: `build` (a command that is safe to run twice), `announce` (a command that posts a message to a channel; posting twice is wrong), `review` (an agent on a model), `approval` (a halt for a release manager), `summarize` (a model call submitted to a batch API and collected later), then it spawns one Smoke unit per platform in a `smoke` lane and waits for them.
- After a restart, a step that completed before the crash is not run again and costs nothing.
- The step that was running at the crash is handled per step, declared by the harness author on the step or the command: rerun it (`build`), never rerun it and park the attempt for the supervisor (`announce`, unless the harness can tell that the post happened, in which case it continues), or ask the step's driver whether it finished (`review`: the agent's session may have completed while the harness was down).
- An `approval` halt resolved while the harness was down is found on restart and the flow continues from it.
- A `summarize` batch submitted before the crash is collected, not resubmitted.
- A resumed attempt is the same attempt: one id, one row in every metric, and the crash is never counted as a model failure or an agent failure.
- Smoke children that finished while the parent was down are seen by the parent on restart; children still running are not restarted.
- An attempt whose flow definition changed between the crash and the restart (a step renamed, a step inserted before the one that was running) is not silently rerun. It is parked for the supervisor with a reason, and the supervisor can restart it from the top or abandon it.
- The harness author writes no resumption code: no checkpoint, no "if already done" branch in a flow, no reading of the ledger from a flow.
- Two copies of the harness started against the same ledger by mistake: the second refuses to start, or takes over from a dead first, and never both run.

## Hostile aspects

- Effects of three kinds (safe to repeat, wrong to repeat, outside the harness's control) in one flow, each with its own restart behaviour, declared by the author and enforced by the kernel.
- State that moved while the harness was down (a halt resolved, a batch completed, a child finished) and must be found, not replayed from memory.
- A definition that changed under a running attempt.
- Single-writer exclusion over a shared ledger.
- Everything above must hold with the ledger as the only kernel state (principle 15), and the author must have nothing to write for it (principle 2).


# Variant format

A variant is a directory. You produce it as a sequence of files, each wrapped exactly like this, with nothing outside the wrappers:

=== FILE: design.md ===
...contents...
=== END ===

Required files:

- `design.md`: the entities (kinds, instances, pivots), the rules, and two mandatory sections: `## What changed and why` (versus the parent; for a seed, versus the brief) and `## Principles broken` (each principle number you knowingly violate, with the reason, or the word "none").
- `h.d.ts`: ambient TypeScript declarations for every module a scenario imports. The kernel is `declare module 'harness-dsl' { ... }`; adapters are `declare module 'harness-dsl/<name>' { ... }`, one block each. `zod` is available as `import { z } from 'zod'` inside the kernel block. These declarations are the DSL: full generics, full inference. `any` in a declaration is counted against you. Keep the surface as small as the battery allows.
- `kernel.d.ts`: the interfaces a backend implements (`Ledger`, `Supplier`, `Store`, `MemoryStore`, `Policy`, `Metrics`, `Client`, and whatever your design needs). Compiled with strict settings. This is what proves the design is implementable. Write it either as a plain module with top-level `export`s, which `h.d.ts` and adapters may import as `'harness-dsl/kernel'`, or as a `declare module 'harness-dsl/kernel' { ... }` block; both resolve.
- The installed zod is **version 4**: `z.ZodType<Output, Input = unknown>` has no `ZodTypeDef` parameter; use `z.infer<typeof schema>` or `z.output<T>` for inferred types. Node globals (`fetch`, `URL`, `Buffer`) are available in scenario files; `process.env` is still forbidden.
- `scenarios/<nn>-<name>.ts`: one file per scenario in the battery, numbered as the battery is, each a complete harness that compiles against `h.d.ts` with `strict: true`, `noImplicitAny: true`, and no `as`, `any`, `!` or `@ts-` anywhere. A scenario you cannot express gets a file containing only a comment that starts `// CANNOT EXPRESS:` followed by the reason; that scores as missing coverage, which is better than a lie.

Rules:

- No comments in `.ts` files other than the `CANNOT EXPRESS` marker. Names carry the meaning.
- Scenario files import only from `harness-dsl`, `harness-dsl/*` and `zod`.
- Every value read from the environment is a reference (`H.env`-shaped), never `process.env`.
- Vendor, product, file-format and tool names appear only inside `harness-dsl/<adapter>` blocks, never inside `declare module 'harness-dsl'`.


# Known weaknesses of the owner's own seed

# Known weaknesses of the seed design (as of 2026-11-01)

These are the gaps I can see without the loop. They are fed to the adversary as "known; find what we did not see", and to mutation as targets.

1. **Flows are coupled to state entities.** `ticketFlow` names `Working`, `Done`, `Abandoned`, so any kind handled by it must own those states. Shared state entities soften this; they do not remove it. Alternative not explored: flows transition to skeleton outcomes and the lane maps them to the kind's states.
2. **`spawn` with `await: true` holds a slot** while children run. The better engine behaviour is that the attempt ends at the spawn and the kind's flow re-enters when children terminate, so an Epic has several attempts. Not designed.
3. **Roles name Claude Code tools** (`.tools(['Read', 'Edit'])`). A role is vocabulary; tool names are a driver's. Should be intents the driver maps.
4. **`.resources()` is path-shaped.** Resources might be entities (`H.resource`) so leases and memory scope can name services, databases, environments, not only globs.
5. **Triggers only fire on transitions.** Time (an SLA breach, a deadline), external events (a customer replied, a PR was merged) and metric thresholds are also sources. Not designed.
6. **Cancellation of active work from outside** (an external event cancels a unit mid-attempt) is not designed. Neither is preemption by the scheduler.
7. **Deadlines, SLAs and per-unit cost ceilings** are not inputs anywhere. Quota is per account; nothing caps what one unit may spend.
8. **Shared accounts across harnesses.** Account quota state lives in each harness's ledger, so two projects sharing a subscription double-count. Account state may need its own shareable backend, separate from the ledger.
9. **The learning loop has no capture entity.** `.record()` lets an agent write, and the supervisor can write; nothing turns outcomes into candidate memories automatically (a failed attempt proposing an experience item). Triggers to journals would do it; the connection is not drawn.
10. **Execution vocabulary is loose.** Run, attempt, invocation, step: four words for levels of execution, used without definitions. The ledger needs them defined.
11. **A handler flow's `.input()` duplicates the lane's kind.** `H.flow.for(Bug)` or the lane supplying the input type would remove the repetition and the chance of mismatch.
12. **Journal reads union across journals of a kind, writes need one destination.** Justified, but asymmetric and unstated in the DSL.
13. **Perpetual units.** A long-lived unit (a running service, a tenancy) that is never terminal does not fit a skeleton of pending/active/terminal. Multi-outcome units (an experiment ending in A, B or inconclusive) fit badly: mapping inconclusive to failed is a lie.
14. **Observers are the one non-entity.** Board and telemetry are functions; alerting (Slack on failure) and webhooks would be more of the same. Possibly fine as "subscriber" shape; possibly a missing noun.
15. **The supervisor's client hides its transport.** A dashboard client would need HTTP, not MCP. Maybe fine; maybe transport is a separate thing.
16. **Startup validation is implicit.** Name collisions (derived descriptors keep their name), transitions outside the kind's states, a trigger on a lane that is not registered: all should fail at `start()`, none is specified.
17. **Journal is the weakest noun in the set.** Curated items are not a journal.

Mechanical scores: compile errors 0, escapes 0, any-in-dts 0, surface 238, coverage 8/10, cannot: none, strikes: none

## Adversary's critique of the parent

## 1. Worst-handled scenario: 02 support triage

The rules hold up in the other scenarios. Here three of them collide.

- **The new message never reaches the redraft.** `customerReplied: H.move(New).from([...AwaitingApproval...])` cancels the attempt and requeues the unit. But `conversationFlow` reads `c.input.latestMessage`, and that comes from store fields. It never reads `c.signals`. The design says signals "only move states", so nothing writes the payload into `latestMessage`. The scenario's "returns to classifying *with the new message*" holds only if Zendesk's store happens to reload. That is a backend accident, not a kernel guarantee.
- **The gate feeds itself.** `skip: { when: safeCategory, decision: { approved: true } }` records a synthetic decision as the `approval` step output. `replyApproval` is defined as `.step(conversationFlow, 'approval').hit(d => d.approved)` and never checks `status: 'skipped'`. So once a category is marked safe, every auto-approval counts as another human approval, and "zero rejections over 200" can never be broken again. A deterministic policy that reads its own output is self-modification by another route (principle 4), and the metric is dishonest (principle 18).
- **Rejection loops forever.** `rejected: New` maps a rejected draft to a pending state. The unit is requeued, re-drafted with no reviewer notes, and rejected again, with no bound.
- **The escalation trigger depends on unstated ordering.** `slaBreachEscalates.where(e => unansweredStates.includes(e.unit.state))` races the lane's own `slaBreach: H.move(Escalated)`. If the move is applied first, `state === 'escalated'` and no Escalation is ever created. The design does not say which runs first.
- **Escalated is excluded from the rate.** `Escalated` is `'concluded'`, so conversation success rate silently drops every escalation.

## 2. New scenario: canary deploy

> **Scenario 9: canary deploy**
>
> Kind Release, supplied by a CI webhook. The handler deploys a canary (command), then samples the error rate for 30 minutes. If the rate exceeds 1%, it runs `rollback` (command), records an experience item, and then halts for a human. Otherwise it runs `promote`, then `verify`.
>
> A Release spawns one Smoke unit per region. The parent proceeds as soon as **any two of three** succeed, and cancels the third.
>
> A trigger whose source is a **metric threshold**: when the Release success rate over 7 days (n ≥ 20) drops below 0.9, a Freeze unit is created. Freeze blocks all new Release starts until it is resolved.
>
> **Hostile aspects:** a branch that runs different steps on each side; a quorum join; a metric as a trigger source.

Why this variant cannot express it:

- **Branching.** The flow has only `.exit(label, when)`, which ends the attempt. A branch where each side runs further steps needs a command that pretends to be the branch, or a second lane reached through a label round-trip.
- **Quorum join.** `spawn` "suspends until all children are terminal". Two-of-three is not possible.
- **Metric trigger.** `H.on` has `transition | streak | step | signal` and nothing metric-based, although principle 13 names metric thresholds explicitly. A schedule-policy hack can block starts, but it cannot *create* the Freeze unit.

## 3. Sharpest critiques

1. **`concluded` is a junk drawer, and outcomes are chosen inconsistently.**
   - *Different meanings, one outcome.* `Escalated`, `Returned` (drafts), `Rejected` (loads), `Parked`, `Churned`, `AWins` and `WeWalkedAway` all map to `'concluded'`. A returned draft is effectively a failed review. An escalation is a support failure. Both drop out of `success()`.
   - *Same meaning, different outcomes.* NightlyLoad `Expired` is `'cancelled'` while Negotiation `Expired` is `'concluded'`.
   - *Terminal states that are not terminal.* `Returned` is terminal and there is no `reopen` reaction. A resubmitted draft is deduped by `key(postId)` and never reviewed again.
2. **One word for four things: `signals`.**
   - `WorkKind.signals()` declares events.
   - `Lane.signals()` declares reactions.
   - `Trigger.signals()` is a consequence.
   - Timers "fire as a signal", and cancellation "is a signal like any other".
   - Then `c.signals` arrives as `readonly SignalRecord[]` with `payload: unknown`. Scenario 8 has to re-validate with `vendorOfferPayload.safeParse`, which throws away the kind's typed declaration. That is an escape hatch in spirit (principle 20).
   - The reaction pivot is `H.move(...)`, a verb, which breaks principle 9.
3. **Hidden coupling through string keys and the ledger.**
   - Metrics and triggers address `'approval'`, `'factCheck'` and `'citations'` by step key on a flow or lane. Rename a step and policies in other files change meaning.
   - `.sets({ category })` makes the flow write into the kind's attribute schema. The flow is supposedly "blind to kinds", yet the lane must type-check the kind against the flow's writes.
   - Quota hangs off the ledger interface (`Ledger.quota: Quota`, with `harnessUtilization` on it). The kernel's "only state" thereby owns a second store, which an `Account` instance can redirect. Scenario 7 works only because each account carries `quota: sharedAccountState`. The ownership question is not answered; the answer depends on which object you happen to read.

## Parent files

=== FILE: design.md ===
# harness-dsl: durable seed

Lens: a unit of work is a durable execution. Its identity (kind + key) outlives processes. Attempts are continuations of it. The ledger is the event history. Timers, signals and children are the normal case, not exceptions.

Temporal's vocabulary was considered and mostly declined:

| Temporal | harness-dsl |
|---|---|
| workflow | **flow** |
| activity | **step** (with an **invocation** per execution) |
| signal | **signal** (kept: no owner word is better for "an event delivered to a unit by id") |
| search attribute | **attribute** |
| child workflow | **spawn** |

## Execution vocabulary (one definition each)

- **Unit**: one piece of work of one kind, identified by `(kind, key)`. It is durable and lives in the ledger. It may also have fields in a store.
- **Attempt**: one pass of the lane's flow over a unit, from start to an end label (or to failure or cancellation).
  - An attempt may **suspend** and later continue. It suspends when blocked on a human, waiting on a timer, waiting on children, or preempted.
  - Suspension is not a new attempt.
  - Statuses: running, blocked, waiting, completed, failed, cancelled.
- **Step**: one named node of a flow. Its output is recorded in the ledger. On resume, recorded outputs are replayed, never re-executed.
- **Invocation**: one execution of an executable inside a step.
  - A retry is a new invocation of the same step.
  - A batch step makes one invocation per item, all sharing a `batchId`.
- There is no "run". The process lifetime is not a domain concept. Restart survival is a property of attempts.

## Entities

### Kinds (vocabulary, no backend)

- `H.state(name, outcome)`: a state entity on the skeleton. Shareable across kinds.
- `H.work(name)`: a work kind.
  - `.attributes()`: typed, indexed, ledger-held scalars that policies and triggers read.
  - `.fields()`: domain data held by the store, if any.
  - `.states([...])`: the first listed state is initial.
  - `.signals({...})`: typed external events the kind accepts.
  - `.timers(t => ...)`: named clocks. Each is a recurrence, a delay from creation, or an attribute holding epoch ms.
  - `.key(fn)`: identity for dedupe and for addressing signals.
- `H.role(name)`:
  - `.intents([...])`: one or more of `read`, `write`, `execute`, `search`, `browse`, `ask`, `remember`. Drivers map intents to their own tools.
  - `.instructions()`, `.input()`, `.output()`.
- `H.memory.experience(name)` / `H.memory.taste(name)`: memory kinds. `.curated()` makes non-owner writes enter as candidates.
- `H.resource(name).paths([...])`: a named thing memory can be scoped to (a service, a database, a path set).
- `H.command(name, argv)`: a deterministic executable. `.parses(shape)` turns stdout JSON into typed `data`.
- `H.flow(name)`: the handler graph (see Flows). Blind to kinds and states.

### Instances (carry a backend; come from adapter subpaths)

Account, model, runner, quota, ledger, store, memory store, supplier, client, projection, external executable.

An instance *is* the kernel interface implementation (`kernel.d.ts`). It is inert until `start()`.

### Pivots (every one names its product)

| Pivot | Composed of | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| **lane** | work kind × suppliers × store × flow × runner | *the place a kind's units are produced, kept and handled* |
| **agent** | role × model (or model choice policy) × pool × journals | *an executable that thinks* |
| **pool** | accounts × shares × preference policy × fallback | *the accounts an agent may draw on* |
| **journal** | memory kind × memory store × recall policy | *where items of a kind are written and how they are recalled* |
| **trigger** | source × consequences | *a recorded firing* |
| **access** | a set of operations | *what a client may do* |
| **harness** | ledger × lanes × triggers × schedule policy × clients × projections | *a running scheduler* |

The lane owns: label→state mapping, flow params, spawn targets, WIP, per-unit budget, signal reactions and preflight.

Policies (`H.policy.schedule|model|account|gate|recall`) and metrics (`H.metric`) are deterministic functions. They are named and never self-modifying.

## Rules

**Skeleton.**
- There are six outcomes: pending, active, succeeded, failed, cancelled, **concluded**. Concluded is terminal and is neither success nor failure.
- Every kind state declares one outcome.
- A unit is in the pending queue *iff* its state's outcome is pending. Nothing else enqueues new attempts.
- A unit in an active state with no open attempt is idle. It holds nothing (a tenancy between reviews, a negotiation awaiting the vendor).

**Success rate.**
- Success rate = succeeded / (succeeded + failed), over units reaching a terminal state in the window.
- `n` = succeeded + failed, and is always returned.
- Cancelled and concluded are excluded from the rate. `metrics.outcomes()` reports them with per-state counts and `share(state)`.
- Example: "how often is an experiment inconclusive" is `outcomes(...).share(Inconclusive)`, with its own `n`.
- The scheduler treats every terminal outcome as terminal.
- "Loaded with warnings" is a succeeded-outcome state distinct from Loaded. It is success to the scheduler and distinct in `byState`.

**Flows emit labels, lanes map labels to states.**
- `.mark(label)` records progress mid-flow.
- `.exit(label, when)` ends the attempt early with `label` when the predicate holds. Later steps never run.
- `.ends(labels, pick)` ends the attempt.
- Every flow implicitly has the label `failed`. It fires on a step failure after retries, when `onFailure` is `'fail'`.
- The lane's `handler(flow, { states: {...} })` must map every label to one of the kind's states. The mapping is typed exhaustively.
- Mapping `failed` to a non-terminal state is allowed (a tenancy review that fails returns to Current).
- One flow serves Bug and Feature; their round counts come from `params`.

**Attributes from a flow.**
- `.sets(shape, make)` records a `unit.attributes` event that updates the unit's attributes (a classifier's category).
- The written keys join the flow's required input. The lane therefore checks at compile time that the kind declares them with matching types.
- `start()` checks that they are attributes, not fields.

**Suspension and capacity.**
- Halts, waits, spawns and preemption suspend the attempt. A suspended attempt:
  - releases its runner slot and account;
  - keeps lane WIP;
  - is persisted.
- Resumption is a queue entry (`reason: 'resume'`) that the scheduler admits like any other.
- Recorded step outputs replay, so a blocked attempt survives restart and resumes at the same step.
- Runner slots and accounts count as capacity only while running. WIP counts open (non-ended) attempts.

**Signals and timers.**
- Suppliers emit either `{ create }` or `{ key, signal, payload }`. A signal addresses an existing unit by key.
- A kind timer fires as a signal of the same name, with payload `{ firedAt }`.
- Timers are queue entries with a future `readyAt`. The scheduler owns the clock, and timers survive restarts.
- A lane reacts to a signal with `H.move(state).from([...])`:
  - the open attempt (if any) is cancelled;
  - the unit moves to the target state;
  - if the target state is pending, the unit is queued.
- `.from` lists the states the reaction applies in. It is typed against the kind's states, independently of the target.
- Signal payloads are recorded and visible to the next attempt as `c.signals`.
- Cancellation is a signal like any other.
- A signal to a unit in a terminal state is rejected unless the reaction's `.from` lists that state.

**Triggers.**
- Sources:
  - `H.on.transition`;
  - `H.on.streak` (N consecutive terminal outcomes per attribute value);
  - `H.on.step` (a recorded step output);
  - `H.on.signal` (including timers).
- Consequences: `.creates(lane)`, `.signals(lane, name)`, `.records(journal)`, `.invokes(executable)`.
- Every source is a recorded ledger event. Every firing is recorded with its source sequence number.
- A flow never names another kind.

**Steps.**
- `step(key, executable, input, { retry, timeoutMs, onFailure, runner })` serves commands, agents and external executables alike.
  - Retry is declared (`H.retry.exponential`) and executed by the engine.
  - `onFailure: 'halt'` turns a failure into a human block carrying the step output.
- `halt(key, { ask, decision, skip })` blocks for a human. `skip.when` is a gate policy; when it returns true, the engine records the given decision instead of blocking (the safe-category rule).
- `batch` submits items as one cloud batch when the agent's model supports it. Its invocations are priced at the batch rate.
- `spawn` creates children through a named outlet, which the lane maps with `H.child(lane, fn)`. It suspends until all children are terminal.
- `loop` repeats a body with typed carry until `again` returns null or the rounds run out.
- An agent with the `ask` intent may halt its own invocation.

**Budget.**
- `lane.budget({ maxUsdPerUnit, onExceed })` caps cumulative invocation cost per unit, across attempts.
- Drivers receive `remainingUsd`.
- Exceeding the cap halts or fails, as declared.

**Memory.**
- The kernel owns the envelope: id, created, kind, status, `when` scope, rule, because, source, mergedFrom.
- Agents `.recalls([...])` journals and `.records(journal)` into one.
  - Reads union all named journals.
  - Writes go to exactly one, because a write needs one destination. The asymmetry is deliberate.
- Recall gives the policy candidates pre-scored by:
  - specificity;
  - track record (present / succeeded attempts);
  - similarity to the step input, when the store supports it.
- The recall policy orders and cuts the candidates deterministically.
- A vector store is a `MemoryStore` that returns similarity.
- Items written by triggers into a `.curated()` kind are candidates until the owner accepts, merges or drops them (`curateMemory`).

**Accounts and quota.**
- By default, quota state is a partition of the ledger (`Ledger.quota`). An account may carry its own `Quota` backend instead.
- Two harnesses that declare the same account with the same quota backend share window and cooldown state.
- Each harness's share cap is per pool, and is checked with `harnessUtilization`.
- Eligibility is read from the quota backend at every decision and never cached across decisions.

**Scheduler.**
- The schedule policy orders candidates (new, resume, timer).
- It may name running attempts to preempt. They suspend at the next invocation boundary and requeue.
- The kernel then admits in order, subject to lane WIP, runner slots, preflight and account eligibility.
- Default policy: FIFO.

**Metrics.**
- Always `{ rate, hits, n }`.
- Built-in: success, outcomes, cost, spend.
- Owner metrics are `H.metric(name).step(flow, key).hit(...)` or `.transition(lane).hit(...)`, computed on demand from recorded events.
- A query naming both `agent` and `model` counts only attempts in which that agent ran that model (`AttemptView.models`).
- Every metric read inside a policy is recorded with the decision (`policy.decided`). A board can therefore show why a model was picked and on how many samples.

**Control API.**
- Clients are granted operations, not capabilities.
- Operations are built-ins (`H.ops.*`) or custom (`H.operation(name).input(...).invokes(executable, prepare)`).
- A client is an adapter that serves `ControlApi` for one `access`.
- Transport (MCP via a coding-agent session, or plain HTTP) is the client's backend.

**Startup validation.** `start()` fails on any of:
- two descriptors with one name;
- a lane whose kind has no states;
- an unmapped label, or a label mapped outside the kind's states;
- a `.sets` key that is a field rather than an attribute;
- a signal reaction or `from` state outside the kind;
- a trigger on an unregistered lane;
- an agent without a model or pool;
- a batch step whose model cannot batch.

`start()` warns on:
- a recurring timer on a kind none of whose lanes react to or trigger on it;
- an access granting an operation for which no client exists.

## Less obvious choices taken

1. Added `concluded` instead of forcing neutral endings onto succeeded or failed.
2. Flows know labels, not states; the lane maps them. This resolves known weaknesses 1 and 11: the flow's `requires` is checked against the kind at the lane.
3. Pending is derived from the state. There is no "re-enter" verb; signals only move states.
4. Halt, wait, spawn and preemption *suspend* the same attempt rather than ending it. The Epic has one attempt that sleeps on its children without holding a slot.
5. Timers are signals. One reaction mechanism covers the SLA breach, the 09:00 cutoff, the two-week expiry and the monthly review.
6. Instances are the backend implementations themselves; there is no descriptor wrapper layer.
7. Quota is a ledger partition that an account may relocate, rather than a second kernel store.
8. Triggers can fire on step outputs, so a command's output can become memory without the command knowing about journals.
9. Agent-initiated halts are an intent (`ask`) that the driver maps.
10. Skills are dropped from memory scope; attributes (e.g. `section`) scope instead.
11. Flows have no branching construct. A single `.exit` covers the cases the battery needs (rejected approval, certificate still valid, too few sources).

## What changed and why

**Versus the brief and the owner's seed:**
- Execution words are defined (weakness 10).
- Attempts suspend and resume (weakness 2, and restart survival).
- Signals and timers are first-class trigger sources and lane reactions (weaknesses 5, 6, 13).
- Cancellation from outside is a signal.
- Per-unit budget and SLA timers exist (weakness 7).
- Quota can be shared across harnesses through an account's quota backend (weakness 8).
- Triggers record memory (weakness 9).
- Roles name intents, not tools (weakness 3).
- Resources are entities (weakness 4).
- Flows are decoupled from states (weakness 1) and from the kind's input (weakness 11).
- The journal read/write asymmetry is stated (weakness 12).
- Perpetual and multi-outcome units fit through idle active states and `concluded` (weakness 13).
- Notifications are external executables invoked by triggers; projections remain the one subscriber shape (weakness 14).
- Transport lives in client adapters (weakness 15).
- Startup validation is specified (weakness 16).
- Journal is kept as the noun (weakness 17 unresolved); curation is an operation on a journal's items.

**Scenario pass (all eight scenarios written against the surface):**
- **`Move` from-states.** `H.move(to).from([...])` previously typed `from` with the target's own state type, so `H.move(New).from([AwaitingApproval])` could not compile. `Move` now carries a separate from-state parameter. The lane checks both the target and the from-states against the kind.
- **`FlowDraft.exit(label, when)`.** Scenario 5 must not load after a rejected approval. Scenario 3 parks before paying for synthesis. Scenario 4 skips renewal when a certificate is still valid. Without an early end, each of these needed a command pretending to be a branch.
- **`FlowDraft.sets(shape, make)`.**
  - Scenario 2's safe-category gate and its "approval rate by category" metric filter on an attribute that only the classifier knows.
  - Attributes could only be set by suppliers.
  - A flow can now write attributes; the lane type-checks the written keys against the kind.
  - The kernel gains the `unit.attributes` ledger event.
- **`H.on.transition` filter.** The filter is typed with `NoInfer`, so the filter list never narrows the lane's inferred state union.
- **`harness-dsl/zendesk.reply`.** An external executable that posts a reply. Sending is an action, not store state.
- **Metric queries.** Naming `agent` and `model` together now has defined semantics (scenario 6 compares two reviewers of one role).
- **Scenario 7.** Scenario files may import only `harness-dsl*`, so its "shared module" is written as the top section of the same file, with both harnesses below it importing nothing but those constants.

## Principles broken

- **12** (five outcomes): the skeleton gains `concluded`.
  - Reason: scenario 8 and the research "parked" outcome cannot be expressed without lying otherwise.
  - Success rate is redefined above: succeeded / (succeeded + failed), with cancelled and concluded excluded from the rate and always reported beside it with their own counts.

=== END ===

declare module 'harness-dsl' {
  import { z } from 'zod';
  import type * as K from 'harness-dsl/kernel';

  type Shape = z.ZodRawShape;
  type Obj<S extends Shape> = z.infer<z.ZodObject<S>>;
  type ScalarShape = { [key: string]: z.ZodType<K.Scalar> };
  type NumberKeys<A> = { [P in keyof A]-?: A[P] extends number ? P : never }[keyof A] & string;

  export type Outcome = K.Outcome;
  export type Terminal = K.Terminal;

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import type { Model } from 'harness-dsl';
import * as claudeCode from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import * as anthropic from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import * as linear from 'harness-dsl/linear';
import * as folder from 'harness-dsl/folder';
import * as sqlite from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import * as jsonl from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import * as git from 'harness-dsl/git';
import * as local from 'harness-dsl/local';
import * as markdown from 'harness-dsl/markdown';

const hourMs = 3_600_000;

const Queued = H.state('queued', 'pending');
const InProgress = H.state('in progress', 'active');
const Done = H.state('done', 'succeeded');
const Abandoned = H.state('abandoned', 'failed');
const Cancelled = H.state('cancelled', 'cancelled');
const ticketStates = [Queued, InProgress, Done, Abandoned, Cancelled];

const ticketAttributes = { priority: z.number(), area: z.string() };
const ticketFields = { title: z.string(), description: z.string(), url: z.string().optional() };

const Bug = H.work('Bug').attributes(ticketAttributes).fields(ticketFields).states(ticketStates);
const Feature = H.work('Feature').attributes(ticketAttributes).fields(ticketFields).states(ticketStates);
const Epic = H.work('Epic')
  .attributes({ priority: z.number() })
  .fields({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() })
  .states(ticketStates);

const Due = H.state('due', 'pending');
const Checking = H.state('checking', 'active');
const Healthy = H.state('healthy', 'succeeded');
const Down = H.state('down', 'failed');
const ServiceHeartbeat = H.work('ServiceHeartbeat')
  .attributes({ service: z.string(), tick: z.number() })
  .states([Due, Checking, Healthy, Down])
  .key(unit => `${unit.attributes.service}@${unit.attributes.tick}`);

const subscriptionA = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-a', { configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_A') });
const subscriptionB = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-b', { configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_B') });
const subscriptionC = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-c', { configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_C') });
const apiAccount = anthropic.account('anthropic-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') });

const soonestExpiring = H.policy.account('soonest-expiring-window', c =>
  [...c.eligible]
    .filter(account => account.eligible && account.harnessUtilization < account.share)
    .sort((a, b) => a.windowEndsAt - b.windowEndsAt)[0] ?? null,
);

const claudePool = H.pool('claude-subscriptions')
  .accounts([
    { account: subscriptionA, share: 0.5 },
    { account: subscriptionB, share: 0.3 },
    { account: subscriptionC, share: 0.2 },
  ])
  .prefer(soonestExpiring)
  .fallback(apiAccount);

const sonnet = claudeCode.model('claude-sonnet-4-5');
const opus = claudeCode.model('claude-opus-4-1');

const builderModel = H.policy.model('builder-model', [sonnet, opus], (c): Model => {
  const cheaper = c.metrics.success({ kind: c.unit ? c.unit.kind : Bug.name, model: sonnet, windowDays: 14 });
  return cheaper.n >= 20 && cheaper.rate !== null && cheaper.rate < 0.85 ? opus : sonnet;
});

const provenShare = (track: { present: number; succeeded: number }): number =>
  track.present === 0 ? 0 : track.succeeded / track.present;

const specificThenProven = H.policy.recall('specific-then-proven', c =>
  [...c.candidates]
    .sort((a, b) => b.specificity - a.specificity || provenShare(b.track) - provenShare(a.track))
    .slice(0, c.limit),
);

const Experience = H.memory.experience('engineering-experience');
const Taste = H.memory.taste('owner-taste');
const experienceJournal = H.journal('experience-journal', Experience)
  .store(jsonl.memory('.harness/memory/experience.jsonl'))
  .recall(specificThenProven);
const tasteJournal = H.journal('taste-journal', Taste)
  .store(jsonl.memory('.harness/memory/taste.jsonl'))
  .recall(specificThenProven);

const builderRole = H.role('builder')
  .intents(['read', 'write', 'execute', 'ask'])
  .instructions('Implement the task in the worktree. Address every listed deficit. Ask the owner when a decision is theirs.')
  .input({ task: z.string(), details: z.string(), deficits: z.array(z.string()) })
  .output({ summary: z.string(), files: z.array(z.string()) });

const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .intents(['read', 'execute', 'remember'])
  .instructions('List every deficit in the change. Record lessons future builders need.')
  .input({ task: z.string(), summary: z.string(), files: z.array(z.string()) })
  .output({ deficits: z.array(z.string()) });

const plannerRole = H.role('planner')
  .intents(['read', 'search'])
  .instructions('Decompose the epic into independently shippable features.')
  .input({ task: z.string(), details: z.string() })
  .output({ features: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() })) });

const projectChecks = H.command('project-checks', ['npm', 'run', 'check']);

const builder = H.agent('builder', builderRole)
  .model(builderModel)
  .pool(claudePool)
  .recalls([experienceJournal, tasteJournal])
  .leaseWrites()
  .mustPass(projectChecks);

const auditor = H.agent('auditor', auditorRole)
  .model(opus)
  .pool(claudePool)
  .recalls([experienceJournal])
  .records(experienceJournal);

const planner = H.agent('planner', plannerRole)
  .model(opus)
  .pool(claudePool)
  .recalls([tasteJournal]);

const deliveryFlow = H.flow('delivery')
  .requires({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() })
  .params({ rounds: z.number() })
  .mark('building')
  .loop(
    'rounds',
    { carry: { deficits: z.array(z.string()) }, rounds: c => c.params.rounds },
    round => round
      .step('build', builder, c => ({
        task: c.input.title,
        details: c.input.description,
        deficits: c.carry ? c.carry.deficits : [],
      }))
      .step('audit', auditor, c => ({ task: c.input.title, summary: c.out.build.summary, files: c.out.build.files })),
    last => (last.audit.deficits.length === 0 ? null : { deficits: last.audit.deficits }),
  )
  .ends(['shipped', 'gaveUp'], c => (c.out.rounds.last.audit.deficits.length === 0 ? 'shipped' : 'gaveUp'));

const decompositionFlow = H.flow('decomposition')
  .requires({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() })
  .mark('planning')
  .step('plan', planner, c => ({ task: c.input.title, details: c.input.description }))
  .spawn('features', {
    outlet: 'feature',
    child: { title: z.string(), description: z.string() },
    items: c => c.out.plan.features,
  })
  .ends(['complete', 'incomplete'], c =>
    c.out.features.every(feature => feature.outcome === 'succeeded') ? 'complete' : 'incomplete',
  );

const healthCheck = H.command('health-check', ['scripts/health-check.sh']);

const heartbeatFlow = H.flow('heartbeat')
  .requires({ service: z.string() })
  .mark('checking')
  .step('check', healthCheck, c => ({ args: [c.input.service] }), { timeoutMs: 30_000 })
  .ends(['healthy'], () => 'healthy');

const tracker = { apiKey: H.env('LINEAR_API_KEY'), team: 'ENG' };
const trackerStatus = {

  done: 'Done',
  abandoned: 'Canceled',

};

const fromIssue = (issue: linear.LinearIssue) => ({

  .signals({ customerReplied: { message: z.string() }, customerClosed: {} })
  .timers(t => ({ slaBreach: t.attribute('slaDueAt') }))
  .key(unit => String(unit.attributes.ticketId));

const EscalationOpen = H.state('escalation open', 'pending');
const EscalationResolved = H.state('escalation resolved', 'succeeded');
const EscalationFailed = H.state('escalation failed', 'failed');

const haiku = anthropic.model('claude-haiku-4-5');
const sonnet = anthropic.model('claude-sonnet-4-5');
const opus = anthropic.model('claude-opus-4-1');

const specificThenProven = H.policy.recall('specific-then-proven', c =>

  .store(jsonl.memory('memory/experience.jsonl'))
  .recall(specificThenProven);

  const cheaper = c.metrics.read(replyApproval, { lane: conversationLane, model: sonnet, windowDays: 30 });
  return cheaper.n >= 50 && cheaper.rate !== null && cheaper.rate < 0.9 ? opus : sonnet;
});

const safeCategory = H.policy.gate('safe-category', (c): boolean => {
  const category = c.unit ? String(c.unit.attributes['category']) : '';
  const approvals = c.metrics.read(replyApproval, { lane: conversationLane, where: { category }, windowDays: 365 });
  return approvals.n >= 200 && approvals.hits === approvals.n;
});

const classifierRole = H.role('classifier')
  .intents(['read'])
  .instructions('Assign the conversation one support category.')
  .input({ subject: z.string(), message: z.string() })

const drafterRole = H.role('drafter')

const classifier = H.agent('classifier', classifierRole).model(haiku).pool(apiAccount);
const drafter = H.agent('drafter', drafterRole)
  .model(drafterModel)

    subject: c.input.subject,
    message: c.input.latestMessage,

  .mark('awaitingApproval')
  .halt('approval', {
    ask: c => `Reply to "${c.input.subject}" (${c.out.classify.category}):\n\n${c.out.draft.reply}`,

  if (event.type === 'ticket.created') return { create: fromTicket(event.ticket) };
  if (event.type === 'comment.added' && event.fromCustomer) {
    return { key: String(event.ticket.id), signal: 'customerReplied', payload: { message: event.ticket.latestComment } };
  }
  if (event.type === 'ticket.solved') return { key: String(event.ticket.id), signal: 'customerClosed', payload: {} };
  return null;
};

const conversationLane = H.lane('conversations', Conversation)
  .supply([

  .signals({

    slaBreach: H.move(Escalated).from([New, Classifying, Drafting, AwaitingApproval]),
  });

const escalationLane = H.lane('escalations', Escalation)
  .handler(escalationFlow, { states: { resolved: EscalationResolved, failed: EscalationFailed } });

const unansweredStates: readonly string[] = [New.name, Classifying.name, Drafting.name, AwaitingApproval.name];

const slaBreachEscalates = H.trigger('sla-breach-escalates', H.on.signal(conversationLane, 'slaBreach'))

const timeToBreach = H.policy.schedule('time-to-breach', c => ({

import { z } from 'zod';

const dailyBudgetUsd = 40;

const Researching = H.state('researching', 'active');
const Delivered = H.state('delivered', 'succeeded');
const Parked = H.state('parked', 'concluded');
const CancelledByOperator = H.state('cancelled by operator', 'cancelled');
const Failed = H.state('failed', 'failed');

const Topic = H.work('Topic')
  .attributes({ recurring: z.boolean() })
  .fields({ question: z.string() })
  .states([Queued, Researching, Delivered, Parked, CancelledByOperator, Failed])
  .signals({ reopen: {}, cancel: {} })
  .key(unit => unit.fields.question);

const apiAccount = anthropic.account('anthropic-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') });
const haikuBatch = anthropic.model('claude-haiku-4-5', { batch: true });
const opus = anthropic.model('claude-opus-4-1');
const sonnet = anthropic.model('claude-sonnet-4-5');

const mostSimilar = H.policy.recall('most-similar', c =>
  [...c.candidates]
    .sort((a, b) => (b.similarity ?? 0) - (a.similarity ?? 0) || b.specificity - a.specificity)
    .slice(0, c.limit),
);
const specificFirst = H.policy.recall('specific-first', c =>
  [...c.candidates].sort((a, b) => b.specificity - a.specificity).slice(0, c.limit),
);

const ReportFindings = H.memory.experience('report-findings');
const SourceExperience = H.memory.experience('source-experience');
const findingsJournal = H.journal('findings-journal', ReportFindings)
  .store(lancedb.memory('memory/findings.lance', { embedding: 'voyage-3' }))
  .recall(mostSimilar);
const sourceJournal = H.journal('source-journal', SourceExperience)
  .store(jsonl.memory('memory/sources.jsonl'))
  .recall(specificFirst);

const synthesizerModel = H.policy.model('synthesizer-model', [opus, sonnet], (c): Model => {
  const first = c.metrics.read(citationPass, { lane: topicLane, model: opus, windowDays: 60 });
  const second = c.metrics.read(citationPass, { lane: topicLane, model: sonnet, windowDays: 60 });
  if (first.n < 15) return opus;
  if (second.n < 15) return sonnet;
  return (first.rate ?? 0) >= (second.rate ?? 0) ? opus : sonnet;
});

const searcherRole = H.role('searcher')
  .intents(['search', 'browse'])
  .instructions('Search for sources on the question from the given angle and extract sourced claims.')
  .input({ question: z.string(), angle: z.number() })
  .output({ sources: z.array(z.object({ url: z.string(), claim: z.string() })) });

const synthesizerRole = H.role('synthesizer')
  .intents(['read', 'remember'])
  .instructions('Write a sourced report. Every claim cites a url from the findings.')
  .input({ question: z.string(), findings: z.array(z.object({ url: z.string(), claim: z.string() })) })
  .output({ report: z.string(), citations: z.array(z.string()), headline: z.string() });

const searcher = H.agent('searcher', searcherRole).model(haikuBatch).pool(apiAccount).recalls([sourceJournal]);
const synthesizer = H.agent('synthesizer', synthesizerRole)
  .model(synthesizerModel)
  .pool(apiAccount)
  .recalls([findingsJournal, sourceJournal])
  .records(sourceJournal);

const citationCheck = H.command('citation-check', ['scripts/check-citations']);
const publishReport = H.command('publish-report', ['scripts/publish-report']);

const researchFlow = H.flow('research')
  .requires({ question: z.string() })
  .mark('researching')
  .batch('search', searcher, c => Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, angle) => ({ question: c.input.question, angle })))
  .exit('parked', c => c.out.search.flatMap(result => result.sources).length < minimumSources)
  .step('synthesize', synthesizer, c => ({
    question: c.input.question,
    findings: c.out.search.flatMap(result => result.sources),
  }))
  .step('citations', citationCheck, c => ({ stdin: JSON.stringify(c.out.synthesize.citations) }))
  .step('publish', publishReport, c => ({ args: [c.input.question], stdin: c.out.synthesize.report }))
  .ends(['delivered'], () => 'delivered');

const topicLane = H.lane('topics', Topic)
  .supply([
    H.supply.operator(),

      c.units
        .filter(unit => unit.attributes.recurring && (unit.outcome === 'succeeded' || unit.outcome === 'concluded'))
        .map(unit => ({ key: unit.key, signal: 'reopen', payload: {} })),
    ),
  ])
  .store(sqlite.store(Topic, 'research.db'))
  .runner(local.shell({ slots: 2 }))
  .handler(researchFlow, {
    states: { researching: Researching, parked: Parked, delivered: Delivered, failed: Failed },
  })
  .budget({ maxUsdPerUnit: 3, onExceed: 'fail' })
  .signals({
    reopen: H.move(Queued).from([Delivered, Parked]),
    cancel: H.move(CancelledByOperator).from([Queued, Researching]),
  });

const citationPass = H.metric('citation-pass').step(researchFlow, 'citations').hit(result => result.exitCode === 0);

          because: `the delivered report on "${event.unit.key}" established it with resolving citations`,

  );

const withinDailyBudget = H.policy.schedule('within-daily-budget', c => {
  const spentUsd = c.metrics.spentUsd({ sinceMs: c.clock.startOfDay('UTC') });
  const projectedUsd = c.metrics.cost({ lane: topicLane, outcome: 'succeeded', windowDays: 30 }).meanUsd ?? 3;
  let remainingUsd = dailyBudgetUsd - spentUsd;
  return {
    start: c.candidates.filter(candidate => {
      if (candidate.entry.reason !== 'start') return true;
      if (projectedUsd > remainingUsd) return false;
      remainingUsd -= projectedUsd;
      return true;
    }),
  };
});

const operatorAccess = H.access('research-operator').allows([
  H.ops.readWork,
  H.ops.createWork,
  H.ops.signalWork,
  H.ops.resolveBlocks,
  H.ops.readMemory,
  H.ops.writeMemory,
  H.ops.readTelemetry,
]);

  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('research-ledger.db'))
  .lanes([topicLane])
  .triggers([deliveredFindingsBecomeMemory])
  .schedule(withinDailyBudget)
  .clients([claudeCode.supervisor('research-supervisor', operatorAccess, { port: H.slot.port(0) })])
  .projections([markdown.board('BOARD.md'), markdown.telemetry('TELEMETRY.md')]);

import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import * as anthropic from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';

const apiAccount = anthropic.account('anthropic-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') });

const opus = anthropic.model('claude-opus-4-1');
const shell = local.shell({ slots: 4 });

const ExperimentScheduled = H.state('experiment scheduled', 'pending');
const Collecting = H.state('collecting', 'active');
const AWins = H.state('a wins', 'concluded');
const BWins = H.state('b wins', 'concluded');
const Inconclusive = H.state('inconclusive', 'concluded');
const ExperimentFailed = H.state('experiment failed', 'failed');
const ExperimentCancelled = H.state('experiment cancelled', 'cancelled');

const Experiment = H.work('Experiment')
  .attributes({ experiment: z.string() })
  .states([ExperimentScheduled, Collecting, AWins, BWins, Inconclusive, ExperimentFailed, ExperimentCancelled])
  .signals({ cancel: {} })
  .key(unit => unit.attributes.experiment);

const sampleMetric = H.command('sample-experiment-metric', ['experiments/sample']);
const decideExperiment = H.command('decide-experiment', ['experiments/decide']).parses({
  winner: z.enum(['a', 'b', 'none']),
});

const experimentFlow = H.flow('experiment')
  .requires({ experiment: z.string() })
  .mark('collecting')
  .loop(
    'hours',
    { carry: {}, rounds: () => 14 * 24 },
    round => round
      .step('sample', sampleMetric, c => ({ args: [c.input.experiment, String(c.round)] }))
      .wait('pause', H.time.after({ hours: 1 })),
    () => ({}),
  )
  .step('decide', decideExperiment, c => ({ args: [c.input.experiment] }))
  .ends(['aWins', 'bWins', 'inconclusive'], c =>
    c.out.decide.data.winner === 'a' ? 'aWins' : c.out.decide.data.winner === 'b' ? 'bWins' : 'inconclusive',
  );

const experimentLane = H.lane('experiments', Experiment)
  .supply([H.supply.operator()])
  .runner(shell)
  .handler(experimentFlow, {
    states: { collecting: Collecting, aWins: AWins, bWins: BWins, inconclusive: Inconclusive, failed: ExperimentFailed },
  })
  .signals({ cancel: H.move(ExperimentCancelled).from([ExperimentScheduled, Collecting]) });

const Current = H.state('current', 'active');
const ReviewDue = H.state('review due', 'pending');
const Suspended = H.state('suspended', 'active');
const Churned = H.state('churned', 'concluded');

const Tenancy = H.work('Tenancy')
  .attributes({ customerId: z.string() })
  .states([Current, ReviewDue, Suspended, Churned])
  .signals({ suspend: {}, reinstate: {}, churn: {} })
  .timers(() => ({ monthlyReview: H.time.monthly(1, '09:00', 'UTC') }))
  .key(unit => unit.attributes.customerId);

const usageReport = H.command('usage-report', ['billing/usage-report']);

const accountReviewerRole = H.role('account-reviewer')
  .intents(['read'])
  .instructions('Summarise the month of usage and whether an upsell conversation is warranted.')
  .input({ customerId: z.string(), usage: z.string() })
  .output({ summary: z.string() });
const accountReviewer = H.agent('account-reviewer', accountReviewerRole).model(sonnet).pool(apiAccount);

const tenancyReviewFlow = H.flow('tenancy-review')
  .requires({ customerId: z.string() })
  .step('usage', usageReport, c => ({ args: [c.input.customerId] }))
  .step('summary', accountReviewer, c => ({ customerId: c.input.customerId, usage: c.out.usage.stdout }))
  .halt('decision', {
    ask: c => `Monthly review for ${c.input.customerId}:\n\n${c.out.summary.summary}\n\nUpsell?`,
    decision: { upsell: z.boolean(), note: z.string() },
