  .ends(['reviewed'], () => 'reviewed');

const billingEvent = z.object({
  customerId: z.string(),
  event: z.enum(['signup', 'suspend', 'reinstate', 'churn']),
});

const tenancyLane = H.lane('tenancies', Tenancy)
  .supply([
    H.supply.operator(),
    http.webhook(Tenancy, { path: '/billing', port: H.slot.port(0), secret: H.env('BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET') }, body => {
      const parsed = billingEvent.safeParse(body);

      const key = parsed.data.customerId;
      switch (parsed.data.event) {
        case 'signup':
          return { create: { attributes: { customerId: key } } };
        case 'suspend':
          return { key, signal: 'suspend', payload: {} };
        case 'reinstate':
          return { key, signal: 'reinstate', payload: {} };
        case 'churn':
          return { key, signal: 'churn', payload: {} };
      }
    }),
  ])
  .store(sqlite.store(Tenancy, 'tenancies.db'))
  .runner(shell)
  .handler(tenancyReviewFlow, { states: { reviewed: Current, failed: Current } })
  .signals({
    monthlyReview: H.move(ReviewDue).from([Current]),
    suspend: H.move(Suspended).from([Current, ReviewDue]),
    reinstate: H.move(Current).from([Suspended]),
    churn: H.move(Churned).from([Current, ReviewDue, Suspended]),
  });

const OurTurn = H.state('our turn', 'pending');
const AwaitingVendor = H.state('awaiting vendor', 'active');
const Agreed = H.state('agreed', 'succeeded');
const WeWalkedAway = H.state('we walked away', 'concluded');
const TheyWalkedAway = H.state('they walked away', 'concluded');
const Expired = H.state('expired', 'concluded');
const NegotiationFailed = H.state('negotiation failed', 'failed');

const Negotiation = H.work('Negotiation')
  .attributes({ vendor: z.string(), expiresAt: z.number() })
  .fields({ item: z.string(), targetPriceUsd: z.number() })
  .states([OurTurn, AwaitingVendor, Agreed, WeWalkedAway, TheyWalkedAway, Expired, NegotiationFailed])
  .signals({ vendorOffered: { offer: z.string() }, vendorWalkedAway: { reason: z.string() } })
  .timers(t => ({ expiry: t.attribute('expiresAt') }))
  .key(unit => `${unit.attributes.vendor}/${unit.fields.item}`);

const negotiatorRole = H.role('negotiator')
  .intents(['read'])
  .instructions('Decide the next move in the procurement negotiation and write the message to the vendor.')
  .input({ vendor: z.string(), item: z.string(), targetPriceUsd: z.number(), vendorOffer: z.string() })
  .output({ move: z.enum(['counter', 'accept', 'walkAway']), message: z.string() });
const negotiator = H.agent('negotiator', negotiatorRole).model(opus).pool(apiAccount);

const sendToVendor = H.command('send-to-vendor', ['procurement/send']);
const vendorOfferPayload = z.object({ offer: z.string() });

const negotiationRoundFlow = H.flow('negotiation-round')
  .requires({ vendor: z.string(), item: z.string(), targetPriceUsd: z.number() })
  .step('offer', negotiator, c => {
    const offers = c.signals
      .filter(signal => signal.name === 'vendorOffered')
      .flatMap(signal => {
        const parsed = vendorOfferPayload.safeParse(signal.payload);
        return parsed.success ? [parsed.data.offer] : [];
      });
    return {
      vendor: c.input.vendor,
      item: c.input.item,
      targetPriceUsd: c.input.targetPriceUsd,
      vendorOffer: offers.length > 0 ? offers[offers.length - 1] : 'no offer yet',

  })
  .step('send', sendToVendor, c => ({ args: [c.input.vendor], stdin: c.out.offer.message }), {
    retry: H.retry.exponential({ maxRetries: 3, initialDelayMs: 30_000 }),
  })
  .ends(['awaitingVendor', 'agreed', 'walkedAway'], c =>
    c.out.offer.move === 'accept' ? 'agreed' : c.out.offer.move === 'walkAway' ? 'walkedAway' : 'awaitingVendor',
  );

const vendorReply = z.object({ negotiation: z.string(), walkAway: z.boolean(), message: z.string() });

const negotiationLane = H.lane('negotiations', Negotiation)
  .supply([
    H.supply.operator(),
    http.webhook(Negotiation, { path: '/vendor-replies', port: H.slot.port(1), secret: H.env('VENDOR_WEBHOOK_SECRET') }, body => {
      const parsed = vendorReply.safeParse(body);
      if (!parsed.success) return null;
      return parsed.data.walkAway
        ? { key: parsed.data.negotiation, signal: 'vendorWalkedAway', payload: { reason: parsed.data.message } }
        : { key: parsed.data.negotiation, signal: 'vendorOffered', payload: { offer: parsed.data.message } };
    }),
  ])
  .store(sqlite.store(Negotiation, 'negotiations.db'))
  .runner(shell)
  .handler(negotiationRoundFlow, {
    states: {
      awaitingVendor: AwaitingVendor,
      agreed: Agreed,
      walkedAway: WeWalkedAway,
      failed: NegotiationFailed,
    },
  })
  .signals({
    vendorOffered: H.move(OurTurn).from([AwaitingVendor]),
    vendorWalkedAway: H.move(TheyWalkedAway).from([OurTurn, AwaitingVendor]),
    expiry: H.move(Expired).from([OurTurn, AwaitingVendor]),

    Number(experimentsOftenInconclusive && candidate.is(experimentLane));
  return { start: [...c.candidates].sort((a, b) => deferred(a) - deferred(b)) };

  H.ops.createWork,
  H.ops.signalWork,
  H.ops.resolveBlocks,
  H.ops.readTelemetry,
]);

export const lifecycles = H.harness('hostile-lifecycles')

# You are designing harness-dsl, a TypeScript DSL for stateful agentic-work harnesses.

# harness-dsl design principles

These are the owner's decisions. A variant that violates one is worse, however elegant. A variant may propose changing one only by stating the principle it breaks and why, in its design notes.

## Vision

1. **Stateless LLMs, stateful harness.** Every model call is a pure function. All state lives in the harness. The harness gets better over time not because models learn but because it feeds the right memory to the right call.
2. **The harness is about work.** Units of work, kinds of work (Bug, Feature, Epic, ServiceHeartbeat, Exercise), hierarchies of kinds, lifecycles, where work comes from, where its state lives, what runs next. The framework is honest about this. It does not hide behind "general purpose".
3. **An LLM is a component, not a requirement.** A harness with zero model calls is a first-class harness. Deterministic scripts and model calls compose through the same executable interface.
4. **Intelligence lives in determinism.** Policies (what to pick, what to recall, what to schedule) are deterministic functions, authored once, reading harness state and metrics at decision time. Policies never change themselves. The harness changes behaviour because policies read changed state.

## Dividing line

5. **Opinionated about shape, agnostic about backend.** The kernel defines what a work unit, a lifecycle, a memory item, a policy, a ledger entry *is*. It never cares where any of them is stored, which vendor serves a model, or which tool the operator uses. Like Eloquent: strict about how you model, indifferent to which database.
6. **Defaults ship, and pass the delete test.** First-party backends ship in the box (SQLite ledger, JSONL memory store, Claude Code driver, folder supplier). Each is one implementation of a public interface. Delete any of them and the kernel still compiles and runs.
7. **`H.*` is kernel vocabulary only.** Shapes and builders. Anything with a backend lives in a subpath (`harness-dsl/claude-code`, `harness-dsl/sqlite`, `harness-dsl/linear`), whether first-party or not. No vendor, CLI, file format or product name appears in `H.*`.
8. **Three sorts of entity.** *Kinds* are pure vocabulary and carry no backend (work kind, state, memory kind, role). *Instances* are specific resources and carry their backend (account, model, runner). *Pivots* connect kinds and instances per harness (pool = accounts × policy, agent = role × model, lane = work kind × suppliers × store × handler, journal = memory kind × store × recall).
9. **Every pivot has a noun.** A pivot enters the DSL only when we can name what it produces. `bind`, `wire`, `attach`, `connect` are not nouns; they are the absence of a concept.
10. **Relationships do not live on kinds.** A work kind does not know who supplies it, stores it or handles it. A role does not know which model runs it. Putting a relationship on a kind makes the kind less reusable.

## Mechanics

11. **Descriptors are immutable and stateless.** Every builder method returns a new descriptor. Nothing is read from the environment at definition time; `H.env('NAME')` and `H.slot.port(n)` are references the runtime resolves. Derived descriptors must be renamed; the runtime refuses two descriptors with one name.
12. **Lifecycle skeleton.** An attempt has one of three outcomes: succeeded, failed, cancelled. This is the harness's track record, and metrics on models, agents, runners and accounts are computed from it. A unit is at one of four positions: pending, active, waiting (parked, holding no capacity, not schedulable), terminal. The scheduler and the board are defined on positions. A kind's named states are entities (shareable); each declares its position, and each terminal state declares its verdict for the kind's own outcome rate: success, failure or neutral, with no default. Blocked (waiting on a human) is an attempt state, not a unit state. A unit outlives its attempts; an attempt's failure moves the unit only where the kind says so. (Amended 2026-11-01 after generation 0: eight of eight variants broke the five-outcome form, and the adversaries showed why.)
13. **Triggers are relationships.** A trigger connects a source (a transition, later also time, external events, metric thresholds) to a consequence (create work in a lane, run an executable, record memory). Flows stay blind to other kinds. Triggers fire only from recorded ledger events and their firings are recorded.
14. **Memory is forward-phrased and atomic.** "Do X when Y because Z", never history. The kernel owns the envelope (id, created, `when`: the kinds, roles, skills and resources an item applies to). Recall is a deterministic policy over items and scope, ranked by specificity and by track record (items present in succeeded attempts rise). Experience (can be wrong, stale, deduped) and taste (the owner's preference, never wrong, broadly scoped) are different kinds.
15. **The ledger is the kernel's only state.** Runs, attempts, invocations, transitions, the pending queue, quota. Its backend is pluggable. There is no kernel work store: domain state lives where the owner's adapter puts it, and a unit may have no store at all.
16. **Supply, store and scheduling are three pillars.** Suppliers produce units (folder, poll, webhook, schedule, operator). Stores hold unit state (one adapter may be both). The scheduler decides what runs next from pending units, lane WIP limits, capacity (runner slots, account eligibility) and a policy. Without a scheduler there is a library, not a harness.
17. **Human-in-the-loop is kernel.** Halting an attempt for an outside decision is universal. Who resolves it, through which surface, is not: the supervisor is one optional client of a control API made of operations, and operations (not capability strings) are what a client is granted.
18. **Metrics are queryable and honest.** Computed from ledger transitions, with sample counts beside every rate, so policy authors write exploration deliberately. Success is defined by the kind's terminal states, never by "the flow finished".

## Ergonomics standards

19. A first-time reader predicts what each line does from its name. Builders chain. Names are nouns for things and verbs for settings. Units sit in names or types (`budgetTokens`, `maxUsd`), never implied.
20. Full inference. Scenario code needs no `as`, `any`, `!` or `@ts-ignore`. A `.d.ts` that uses `any` to make inference "work" fails this standard.
21. Small surface. The fewest entities and methods that express the whole scenario battery without escape hatches. An entity with one use is suspect. A method nobody in the battery calls is removed.
22. No two words for one thing. Run, attempt, invocation, step have one definition each, or fewer words.


# Scenario battery

# Scenario 1: coding team

A product team's harness, the shape harness-dsl was first built for.

## Must express

- Three kinds of work in a hierarchy: Epic decomposes into Features; Bugs arrive on their own. Epic completes when its Features do. Feature and Bug share most of their lifecycle and handler but differ in how many build-and-audit rounds they get (Bug 3, Feature 5).
- Supply from three places at once for Bugs: an issue tracker (Linear), a folder of markdown files, and the operator typing to the supervisor. Features from the tracker and the operator. Epics from the tracker only.
- Bug and Feature state is kept in the tracker; the harness is not the source of truth for them.
- A builder agent on a worktree per attempt, with a file-lease guard (two attempts may not write the same file) and a stop check that runs the project's checks before the agent may stop.
- An auditor agent that finds deficits; the loop continues until none remain or rounds run out. The builder may halt the attempt for an owner decision.
- Accounts: three Claude subscriptions in a pool with per-account quota shares, drained soonest-expiring first, falling back to an API account. Model choice for the builder reads the ledger: use the cheaper model until its success rate on this kind of work, over 14 days and at least 20 samples, drops below 0.85.
- Memory: experience ("when touching payments, run the ledger fixture first, because the migration reorders rows") recalled by builder and auditor, recorded by the auditor; taste ("prefer early returns over nested conditionals") recalled by builder and planner, written by the owner.
- A service heartbeat every five minutes, all deterministic, whose failure creates a Bug through a trigger. The heartbeat flow must not reference the Bug kind.
- Scheduler: heartbeats first, then bugs, features, epics; a WIP limit of 2 concurrent bugs and 1 epic; starvation protection for features.
- Supervisor: a Claude Code session granted read and write on work, blocker resolution, memory writes, telemetry and account shares, plus one custom operation (a production health probe).
- Board and telemetry projections written as Markdown files.

## Hostile aspects

- The heartbeat kind must have no store and must still appear in telemetry.
- The same handler flow serves two kinds with different round counts without duplication.
- The model-choice policy must expose sample counts; a variant that hides them fails.


---

# Scenario 2: support triage

Customer conversations arrive from a helpdesk webhook. Nothing here touches files.

## Must express

- One kind of work, Conversation, supplied by a webhook (push) and by a periodic poll of the helpdesk for anything the webhook missed. State lives in the helpdesk via its API; the harness holds nothing but its ledger.
- Lifecycle: new, classifying, drafting, awaiting approval, sent, closed by customer, escalated. A human approves every outgoing reply (halt), except for a category the policy marks safe after 200 approved samples with zero rejections.
- Two agents: a classifier on a cheap model, a drafter on a stronger one. The drafter recalls taste (tone, phrases to avoid) and experience ("when the customer mentions a refund older than 30 days, cite policy 4.2"). A reviewer role (human, through the supervisor) records taste from its edits.
- Deadlines: each conversation carries an SLA; the scheduler orders by time to breach, not by arrival. A breached SLA fires a trigger that escalates (creates an Escalation unit in another lane with its own handler and a human-only flow).
- External cancellation: if the customer replies while a draft is awaiting approval, the attempt is cancelled and the unit returns to classifying with the new message.
- Per-unit cost ceiling: no conversation may spend more than $0.40 of model cost; a unit that would exceed it halts for a human.
- Metrics the policy reads: approval rate by category and by model, with sample counts.

## Hostile aspects

- Cancellation from outside an active attempt.
- A trigger whose source is time (SLA breach), not a transition.
- A cost ceiling scoped to a unit, not an account.
- A lane whose handler contains no model call at all (Escalation).


---

# Scenario 3: research pipeline

A team runs literature-style research: a topic goes in, a sourced report comes out.

## Must express

- Kind Topic, supplied by the operator and by a weekly schedule that re-opens topics tagged "recurring". Topics are stored in the harness's own store (no external system), so the first-party store is the right choice here.
- Handler: fan out 20 search-and-extract calls as one cloud batch on a cheap model (the batch API discount matters), gather, then one synthesis call on a strong model, then a deterministic citation check command that fails the attempt if a citation does not resolve.
- Memory with a vector-store backend: prior report findings are a memory kind recalled by the synthesizer by semantic similarity. Recall is still a deterministic policy; the vector store is a backend. Experience about sources ("when the source is a preprint server, downgrade confidence") is a second kind in a JSONL store.
- Per-topic cost ceiling of $3; the scheduler never starts a topic whose projected cost (from the metric: mean cost of succeeded attempts of this kind) would pass the remaining daily budget of $40.
- Outcome: a report is delivered, or the topic is parked (not enough sources), or it is cancelled by the operator. Parked is not failure.
- The synthesizer's model is chosen by a policy that compares two strong models on a metric the owner defines: citation-check pass rate.

## Hostile aspects

- A memory backend that is not a file and a recall policy that uses similarity, while recall stays deterministic.
- A cloud batch step inside a flow, priced at the batch discount in telemetry.
- Budget as a scheduling input (daily, across units).
- A terminal outcome, parked, that is neither success nor failure.


---

# Scenario 4: operations, no model anywhere

A platform team uses the harness purely as a durable scheduler of deterministic work. There is no model, no account, no agent in this harness. If a variant needs any of them to compile or start, it fails the scenario.

## Must express

- Kinds: Heartbeat (every 5 minutes per service), Backup (nightly per database), CertificateRenewal (weekly check, act when under 14 days), Incident (created by triggers, handled by a runbook flow that pages a human and waits).
- Suppliers: schedules only, plus the operator creating Incidents by hand through the control API over plain HTTP (no Claude Code, no MCP).
- Runners: local for heartbeats; SSH to two hosts for backups and renewals, with per-host concurrency of 1 and a disk-space preflight.
- Triggers: three consecutive failed heartbeats of one service create an Incident (a trigger over a pattern of transitions, not a single transition). A failed Backup creates an Incident at once. A Backup that succeeded but took over 2 hours records a note in a journal of operational experience, which is also a memory kind, even though nothing here reads memory into a prompt; the supervisor reads it.
- The Incident flow halts for a human acknowledgement, then runs a runbook command, then halts for a human to confirm resolution.
- Scheduler: Incidents preempt everything; a running Backup is not interrupted, but no new Backup starts while an Incident is active.
- Observers: a Slack notification on every Incident transition, and the board file.

## Hostile aspects

- Zero model calls: every executable is a command.
- A trigger whose source is a pattern across several transitions.
- Preemption rules in the scheduler.
- A control API client that is plain HTTP.
- A memory kind with no agent reading it.


---

# Scenario 5: data job with approval

A nightly data job with one human gate in the middle and a retry policy.

## Must express

- Kind NightlyLoad, supplied by a schedule at 02:00, one unit per source system (four). State in the harness's store.
- Handler: extract (command, SSH runner), validate (command), then a model call that writes a plain-language summary of anomalies, then halt for a human to approve the load, then load (command), then verify (command).
- Retry: extract and load retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff on failure, as a policy on the step, not hand-written in the command. A validation failure does not retry; it halts for a human with the validation report.
- Outcome: loaded, loaded with warnings (verify found tolerable drift), rejected by the approver, or failed. Loaded with warnings is a success for scheduling purposes but must be distinguishable in metrics and on the board.
- A unit left waiting for approval past 09:00 is cancelled by a time trigger and a new one is not created until the next night.
- Resumability: if the harness process restarts while a unit is blocked on approval, the unit is still blocked after restart and resumes at the same step when approved.
- The approver works through the supervisor; the summary agent recalls taste about what the approver wants emphasised.

## Hostile aspects

- Retry with backoff as a declared policy on a step.
- Restart survival of a blocked attempt.
- A success-with-warnings outcome that is success to the scheduler and distinct to metrics.
- A time trigger that cancels, scoped to one kind.


---

# Scenario 6: content review driven by taste

A publication runs drafts through review. The point of this harness is that it learns the owner's taste.

## Must express

- Kind Draft, supplied from a CMS by poll, state in the CMS.
- Handler: two reviewer agents on two different models each produce a critique; a deterministic command merges them; the editor (human, supervisor) accepts or returns the draft with notes.
- Taste memory grows from the editor's notes: every returned draft's notes become candidate taste items through a trigger (returned → record taste candidate), curated by the editor later through the control API (accept, merge, drop). Reviewers recall taste; taste applies to all drafts, with a smaller set scoped to a section (`sports`, `opinion`).
- A/B on models: the two reviewers' models are chosen by a policy that reads which reviewer's critiques the editor acted on more (a metric the owner defines from editor actions recorded as transitions), with sample counts, and swaps the weaker model after 50 samples.
- Experience memory also exists (fact-checking lessons), recalled by both reviewers, recorded by the fact-check command when it finds a repeat mistake.
- No worktrees, no files, no code.

## Hostile aspects

- Memory capture as a trigger consequence, not an agent tool.
- Curation operations on memory (merge, drop) exposed to the supervisor.
- A metric defined by the owner from recorded operator actions, not from attempt outcomes.
- Two agents of the same role on different models in one flow.


---

# Scenario 7: two projects, shared subscriptions

The owner runs two independent product harnesses (two repositories, two ledgers, two supervisors) that share the same three Claude subscription accounts.

## Must express

- Each harness declares the same three accounts. Account quota state (utilization windows, cooldowns) is shared between the two harnesses: if harness A drives an account into cooldown, harness B sees it. Project share caps are per harness: A may use 60% of an account's window, B 30%.
- Each harness has its own ledger (runs, attempts, telemetry) in its own SQLite file. Neither can see the other's runs.
- Fair scheduling across tenants is not the kernel's job (they are separate processes), but each scheduler must respect account eligibility that the other may have changed a second ago.
- Harness A is the coding team of scenario 1. Harness B is a documentation harness: kind DocPage, supplied from a folder, handled by a writer agent and a link-check command, stored in the folder's frontmatter.
- A shared taste journal: both harnesses recall the owner's taste from one JSONL file; each has its own experience journal.
- The owner's one supervisor session can be pointed at either harness (two control API endpoints) and sees the shared account state from both.

## Hostile aspects

- Account state that outlives and spans harnesses: where does it live, and is that a second kernel store or a backend of the ledger?
- Two ledgers, one memory store, three shared accounts: the design must say which entity owns which state without new ad-hoc concepts.
- The same entity definitions (accounts, taste journal) imported by two harness files from a shared module.


---

# Scenario 8: lifecycles that do not fit

Three kinds of work chosen to break a pending/active/succeeded/failed/cancelled skeleton. A variant must express them without lying: mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean is a failure of this scenario.

## Must express

- **Experiment**: an A/B test unit runs for two weeks, collecting a metric from a command every hour. It ends in one of: A wins, B wins, inconclusive. None of these is failure. The scheduler must treat all three as terminal; metrics must distinguish them; a policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how often are experiments inconclusive?"
- **Tenancy**: a customer's tenancy is a unit of work that is never terminal while the customer is a customer. It is re-evaluated monthly (usage review, a model-written summary, a human decision to upsell or not) and may be suspended and reinstated any number of times. It ends only on churn, which is neither success nor failure. The scheduler must not consider an active tenancy as occupying capacity between evaluations.
- **Negotiation**: a procurement negotiation unit alternates between the harness (an agent drafts the next offer) and the outside world (the vendor replies, via a webhook supplier that updates an existing unit rather than creating one). It may end in agreement, walk-away by us (a decision, not a failure), walk-away by them, or expiry (a time trigger). Each attempt is one round; the unit outlives many attempts.

## Hostile aspects

- Terminal states that are neither success nor failure, needed by metrics.
- A unit that is active for years and must not hold capacity.
- A supplier that updates an existing unit instead of creating one.
- An attempt-per-round model where the unit's identity spans attempts and external replies.
- If the variant changes the skeleton (adds outcomes, replaces the five with something else), its design notes must say what success rate means afterwards.


---

# Scenario 9: a harness watching itself

The support harness of scenario 2 observes its own metrics and acts on them. Nothing here is new work from outside; every unit created here is created by the harness about itself.

## Must express

- A trigger whose source is a metric threshold: when the approval rate for a category over the last 7 days falls below 0.9 with at least 50 samples, the harness creates one Audit unit for that category in an `audits` lane with a human-only handler. While an Audit for that category is open, no second one is created, however many samples cross the threshold.
- The same crossing records a candidate experience item scoped to the drafter role and the category: "when drafting for {category}, recall the stricter phrasing, because approvals fell to {rate}".
- When the category's rate recovers above 0.95, the open Audit is cancelled. Below 0.9 and above 0.95 are two thresholds on purpose: the trigger fires on a crossing, once, not on every sample.
- A trigger that pauses the `conversations` lane when the harness's own model error rate over the last hour exceeds 0.2 with at least 20 invocations, and resumes it when the rate falls below 0.05. Paused means: nothing new starts in the lane, running attempts finish. Both the pause and the resume are recorded on the ledger and visible on the board, with the metric value that caused them.
- Each conversation's SLA can be extended by the reviewer through the supervisor. The breach timer moves with the new deadline; the old deadline never fires.
- A policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how many Audits were opened per category this month" and "how long was the lane paused in total".

## Hostile aspects

- A trigger source that is a metric, not a transition, a time or an external event; it still fires only from recorded ledger state and its firings are recorded.
- Hysteresis: two thresholds, one firing per crossing.
- Deduplication by a group key (the category), not by kind.
- A consequence that acts on a lane, not on a unit, and is itself a recorded, queryable fact.
- A timer whose deadline changes after it was armed.


---

# Scenario 10: the power goes off

A release harness is killed mid-attempt (power cut, OOM, `kill -9`, laptop closed) and started again. This scenario states what must be true after the restart. It does not say how; a variant that satisfies every line by any mechanism passes, and its design.md must name the mechanism and what the harness author had to write for it.

## Must express

- Kind Release, supplied by the operator. Its flow, in order: `build` (a command that is safe to run twice), `announce` (a command that posts a message to a channel; posting twice is wrong), `review` (an agent on a model), `approval` (a halt for a release manager), `summarize` (a model call submitted to a batch API and collected later), then it spawns one Smoke unit per platform in a `smoke` lane and waits for them.
- After a restart, a step that completed before the crash is not run again and costs nothing.
- The step that was running at the crash is handled per step, declared by the harness author on the step or the command: rerun it (`build`), never rerun it and park the attempt for the supervisor (`announce`, unless the harness can tell that the post happened, in which case it continues), or ask the step's driver whether it finished (`review`: the agent's session may have completed while the harness was down).
- An `approval` halt resolved while the harness was down is found on restart and the flow continues from it.
- A `summarize` batch submitted before the crash is collected, not resubmitted.
- A resumed attempt is the same attempt: one id, one row in every metric, and the crash is never counted as a model failure or an agent failure.
- Smoke children that finished while the parent was down are seen by the parent on restart; children still running are not restarted.
- An attempt whose flow definition changed between the crash and the restart (a step renamed, a step inserted before the one that was running) is not silently rerun. It is parked for the supervisor with a reason, and the supervisor can restart it from the top or abandon it.
- The harness author writes no resumption code: no checkpoint, no "if already done" branch in a flow, no reading of the ledger from a flow.
- Two copies of the harness started against the same ledger by mistake: the second refuses to start, or takes over from a dead first, and never both run.

## Hostile aspects

- Effects of three kinds (safe to repeat, wrong to repeat, outside the harness's control) in one flow, each with its own restart behaviour, declared by the author and enforced by the kernel.
- State that moved while the harness was down (a halt resolved, a batch completed, a child finished) and must be found, not replayed from memory.
- A definition that changed under a running attempt.
- Single-writer exclusion over a shared ledger.
- Everything above must hold with the ledger as the only kernel state (principle 15), and the author must have nothing to write for it (principle 2).


# Variant format

A variant is a directory. You produce it as a sequence of files, each wrapped exactly like this, with nothing outside the wrappers:

=== FILE: design.md ===
...contents...
=== END ===

Required files:

- `design.md`: the entities (kinds, instances, pivots), the rules, and two mandatory sections: `## What changed and why` (versus the parent; for a seed, versus the brief) and `## Principles broken` (each principle number you knowingly violate, with the reason, or the word "none").
- `h.d.ts`: ambient TypeScript declarations for every module a scenario imports. The kernel is `declare module 'harness-dsl' { ... }`; adapters are `declare module 'harness-dsl/<name>' { ... }`, one block each. `zod` is available as `import { z } from 'zod'` inside the kernel block. These declarations are the DSL: full generics, full inference. `any` in a declaration is counted against you. Keep the surface as small as the battery allows.
- `kernel.d.ts`: the interfaces a backend implements (`Ledger`, `Supplier`, `Store`, `MemoryStore`, `Policy`, `Metrics`, `Client`, and whatever your design needs). Compiled with strict settings. This is what proves the design is implementable. Write it either as a plain module with top-level `export`s, which `h.d.ts` and adapters may import as `'harness-dsl/kernel'`, or as a `declare module 'harness-dsl/kernel' { ... }` block; both resolve.
- The installed zod is **version 4**: `z.ZodType<Output, Input = unknown>` has no `ZodTypeDef` parameter; use `z.infer<typeof schema>` or `z.output<T>` for inferred types. Node globals (`fetch`, `URL`, `Buffer`) are available in scenario files; `process.env` is still forbidden.
- `scenarios/<nn>-<name>.ts`: one file per scenario in the battery, numbered as the battery is, each a complete harness that compiles against `h.d.ts` with `strict: true`, `noImplicitAny: true`, and no `as`, `any`, `!` or `@ts-` anywhere. A scenario you cannot express gets a file containing only a comment that starts `// CANNOT EXPRESS:` followed by the reason; that scores as missing coverage, which is better than a lie.

Rules:

- No comments in `.ts` files other than the `CANNOT EXPRESS` marker. Names carry the meaning.
- Scenario files import only from `harness-dsl`, `harness-dsl/*` and `zod`.
- Every value read from the environment is a reference (`H.env`-shaped), never `process.env`.
- Vendor, product, file-format and tool names appear only inside `harness-dsl/<adapter>` blocks, never inside `declare module 'harness-dsl'`.


# Known weaknesses of the owner's own seed

# Known weaknesses of the seed design (as of 2026-11-01)

These are the gaps I can see without the loop. They are fed to the adversary as "known; find what we did not see", and to mutation as targets.

1. **Flows are coupled to state entities.** `ticketFlow` names `Working`, `Done`, `Abandoned`, so any kind handled by it must own those states. Shared state entities soften this; they do not remove it. Alternative not explored: flows transition to skeleton outcomes and the lane maps them to the kind's states.
2. **`spawn` with `await: true` holds a slot** while children run. The better engine behaviour is that the attempt ends at the spawn and the kind's flow re-enters when children terminate, so an Epic has several attempts. Not designed.
3. **Roles name Claude Code tools** (`.tools(['Read', 'Edit'])`). A role is vocabulary; tool names are a driver's. Should be intents the driver maps.
4. **`.resources()` is path-shaped.** Resources might be entities (`H.resource`) so leases and memory scope can name services, databases, environments, not only globs.
5. **Triggers only fire on transitions.** Time (an SLA breach, a deadline), external events (a customer replied, a PR was merged) and metric thresholds are also sources. Not designed.
6. **Cancellation of active work from outside** (an external event cancels a unit mid-attempt) is not designed. Neither is preemption by the scheduler.
7. **Deadlines, SLAs and per-unit cost ceilings** are not inputs anywhere. Quota is per account; nothing caps what one unit may spend.
8. **Shared accounts across harnesses.** Account quota state lives in each harness's ledger, so two projects sharing a subscription double-count. Account state may need its own shareable backend, separate from the ledger.
9. **The learning loop has no capture entity.** `.record()` lets an agent write, and the supervisor can write; nothing turns outcomes into candidate memories automatically (a failed attempt proposing an experience item). Triggers to journals would do it; the connection is not drawn.
10. **Execution vocabulary is loose.** Run, attempt, invocation, step: four words for levels of execution, used without definitions. The ledger needs them defined.
11. **A handler flow's `.input()` duplicates the lane's kind.** `H.flow.for(Bug)` or the lane supplying the input type would remove the repetition and the chance of mismatch.
12. **Journal reads union across journals of a kind, writes need one destination.** Justified, but asymmetric and unstated in the DSL.
13. **Perpetual units.** A long-lived unit (a running service, a tenancy) that is never terminal does not fit a skeleton of pending/active/terminal. Multi-outcome units (an experiment ending in A, B or inconclusive) fit badly: mapping inconclusive to failed is a lie.
14. **Observers are the one non-entity.** Board and telemetry are functions; alerting (Slack on failure) and webhooks would be more of the same. Possibly fine as "subscriber" shape; possibly a missing noun.
15. **The supervisor's client hides its transport.** A dashboard client would need HTTP, not MCP. Maybe fine; maybe transport is a separate thing.
16. **Startup validation is implicit.** Name collisions (derived descriptors keep their name), transitions outside the kind's states, a trigger on a lane that is not registered: all should fail at `start()`, none is specified.
17. **Journal is the weakest noun in the set.** Curated items are not a journal.

# Parent variant (g00-minimal-0)

Mechanical scores: compile errors 0, escapes 0, any-in-dts 0, surface 175, coverage 8/10, cannot: none, strikes: none

## Adversary's critique of the parent

## 1. Worst-handled scenario: 8 (lifecycles that do not fit)

Scenario 8 forbids lies. This variant tells several.

**Negotiation maps failure onto a state that means something else.**
- `if (!proposal.ok) return 'vendor-replied';` and `if (!sent.ok) return 'vendor-replied';`
- A model or mail failure is recorded as "the vendor replied." This is a `pending`-mapped state, so the unit loops forever with no failure counted.
- The ledger transition says `cause: 'flow'`, `to: 'vendor-replied'`. Metrics on rounds-per-negotiation are now wrong.

**Tenancy suspension races the wake condition.**
- `ctx.until('current', { at: +30d, then: 'review-due' })` arms a wake.
- The billing webhook then moves the unit to `suspended`. Rule 5 and Rule 7 never say whether a supplier move clears `wakeAt`.
- A suspended tenancy may wake into `review-due` on day 30 and be reviewed while suspended.

**Experiment silently swallows measurement failures.**
- `sample.ok ? [...] : ctx.unit.data.observations` drops a failed hourly sample with no record.
- The experiment can end `inconclusive` from missing data, and nothing distinguishes that from a genuine tie.

**The same pattern recurs in scenario 2.**
- `if (!classified.ok) return 'escalated';` reaches an `ended` state named "escalated", but no Escalation unit is created.
- `escalated` therefore has two meanings: a real SLA escalation, and "the classifier crashed."

## 2. New scenario: canary rollout

*Scenario 9: canary rollout*

A `Deploy` kind is supplied by a webhook from CI and handled by deterministic commands only.

**Must express**
- Rollout runs as 5% → 25% → 100%. Each stage waits 20 minutes, then reads the error rate from a probe command.
- If the error rate of `Deploy` invocations tagged `stage=canary` exceeds 0.02 over the last hour, with at least 30 samples, a trigger:
  - creates a `Rollback` unit in another lane;
  - pauses all pending `Deploy` units.
- The probe command hangs in practice. Any invocation exceeding 10 minutes is killed, counted as failed, and the runner slot is freed.
- A deploy for service X must not start while a `Rollback` for X is active, keyed by service, not by kind.

**Hostile aspects**
- **A trigger whose source is a metric threshold.** `H.on` offers only `enters | streak | deadline | clock`.
  - The only workaround is a schedule policy that filters `start`. That policy cannot create the `Rollback` unit, because policies return orderings and not effects.
  - Faking it with `clock` plus a flow that polls metrics means a flow reading `Metrics`, which `FlowContext` does not expose. Metrics are only reachable through `ctx.decide`, a misuse of the rule policy.
- **A per-invocation timeout.** The design notes list "`timeout`: removed." A hung probe therefore holds its runner slot indefinitely, and nothing in `RunOptions` can bound it.
- **Exclusion keyed by a resource, not a kind.** There is no resource entity ("strings in scopes and leases"). The policy must compare `unit.data.service` strings across kinds by hand.

## 3. Three sharpest critiques

**a. "schedule" names three different things, breaking principle 22.**
- `H.schedule(...)` is a supplier.
- `H.policy.schedule(...)` is the scheduler.
- `.scheduler(policy)` is the harness setting.
- `H.on.clock(..., { daily })` and `TimeSpec` are a fourth time-based mechanism.

A newcomer reading `H.schedule('two-am', ...)` and `H.policy.schedule('daily-budget', ...)` side by side cannot tell which one decides what runs next. Separately, `ctx.halt` and `ModelResponse { status: 'asked' }` with `Intent 'ask'` are two mechanisms for one concept. Scenario 1's builder works around this with an output field `question`.

**b. Kind data carries runner identity, breaking principles 8 and 10.**
- In scenario 4, `databases = [{ database: 'orders', host: hostA.name }]` puts the backup's host into the kind's data.
- `hostFor = input => input.host === hostA.name ? hostA : hostB` then resolves runners by string comparison.
- The kind `Backup` (vocabulary) now knows an instance's name. A typo silently routes to `hostB`, and startup validation (Rule 15) cannot catch it.
- The same raw-string-for-entity pattern appears in `resources: ['section:sports']` and `'payments'`. This is exactly the seed's W4, left unfixed and listed as "cut."

**c. `Ledger extends QuotaBook` conflates two owners of state, bending principle 15.**
- Rule 11 says quota lives "by default" in the ledger and otherwise in `sqlite.quota(path)`. So the ledger is both the kernel's only state and, sometimes, not the home of quota.
- Accounts select their book through a vendor-subpath option: `claudeCode.subscription(..., { quota })`.
- Nothing stops one account from being declared with a shared book in harness A and the default ledger book in harness B. That silently reintroduces scenario 7's double-counting.
- Because `QuotaBook` is an interface the ledger implements rather than a named pivot, principle 9 is also strained. The design never says what account state is part of.

## Parent files

=== FILE: design.md ===
# harness-dsl: minimal seed

This design uses the smallest surface I can defend against the eight scenarios. I started from the assumption that eight nouns are too many. The battery forced back the ones listed below. Each entity that stays has at least one scenario that cannot be written without it.

## Entities

| Sort | Entity | Builder | Produces / is |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kind | **kind** | `H.kind(n).data(z).states(map, initial)` | The vocabulary of one sort of work: a data shape plus a lifecycle. |
| Kind | **role** | `H.role(n).input(z).output(z).prompt(f).intents([...])` | What a model call is asked to do. It names intents, not tool names. |
| Kind | **memory** | `H.memory(n, 'fallible' \| 'owner').data(z?)` | A memory kind. Experience is `fallible`; taste is `owner`. |
| Instance | account, model, runner, store, memory store, supplier, ledger, quota book, guard, observer, client | adapters only | Specific resources that carry their backend. |
| Pivot | **agent** | `H.agent(n, role).model(m \| policy)` | An executable: role × model. |
| Pivot | **lane** | `H.lane(n, kind).handler(flow, params).suppliers(...).store(s).wip(n).maxUsdPerUnit(x)` | A work queue: kind × suppliers × store × handler. |
| Pivot | **library** | `H.library(n, memory, store).recall(policy)` | The recall source for one memory kind: memory kind × store × recall. |
| Pivot | **pool** | `H.pool(n, members, accountPolicy)` | The account that serves a call: accounts × shares × policy. |
| Pivot | **trigger** | `H.trigger(n, source, (event, act) => effects)` | A recorded consequence of a recorded source. |
| Composite | **flow** | `H.flow(n).for(...kinds).params(z).does(async ctx => state)` | A handler body. |
| Composite | **command** | `H.command(n).input(z).output(z).argv(f).on(runner)` | A deterministic executable. |
| Composite | **policy** | `H.policy.{model,account,schedule,recall,retry,rule}(n, fn)` | One entity with six decision shapes. |
| Composite | **operation** | `H.ops.*`, `H.operation(n, exec)` | A grantable unit of the control API. |
| Root | **harness** | `H.harness(n).ledger(l).lanes(...).pools(...).triggers(...).scheduler(p).clients(...).observers(...)` | The running thing. |

Some things are plain values, not entities, and are never registered:

- `H.lifecycle(map)`
- `Scope`
- `TimeSpec`
- `H.env(name)` and `H.slot.port(n)`
- `H.schedule(...)` and `H.operator`. These two are suppliers with no backend, because the clock and the control API are kernel.
- `DataOf<K>` and `StateOf<K>`. These are type helpers only.

## Execution vocabulary (one definition each)

- **Run**: one lifetime of a harness process, from `start()` until `stop()` or a crash. It is recorded as `run` entries.
- **Attempt**: one execution of a lane's flow for one unit.
  - A unit has zero or more attempts.
  - An attempt is `running`, `blocked` (halted, waiting on a human), or `ended` with succeeded, failed or cancelled.
  - The attempt's outcome describes the execution. The unit's state describes the work.
- **Invocation**: one call of one executable inside an attempt. A retry is a new invocation. Each item of a batch is its own invocation.
- **Step**: not a word in this design. It is removed.

## Rules

### 1. Lifecycle skeleton (a replacement; see Principles broken)

There are seven outcomes:

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pending` | Schedulable now. |
| `active` | An attempt is running or blocked. |
| `idle` | Resting. The unit holds no capacity and is not schedulable. It wakes by time, by its children ending, by a supplier update, by a trigger or by an operation. |
| `succeeded` | Terminal. |
| `failed` | Terminal. |
| `cancelled` | Terminal. |
| `ended` | Terminal, and neither success nor failure. |

A kind maps each named state to one outcome. States are not entities: a lifecycle is a plain map. Triggers address `(kind, stateName)`.

### 2. Success rate is `hits / samples`

- Hits are units entering a `succeeded`-mapped state.
- Samples are units entering a `succeeded`- or `failed`-mapped state.
- `ended` and `cancelled` are excluded from the denominator. They are always countable by state name through `rate` and `rateBy`.
- "Loaded with warnings" is a separate `succeeded` state. It is success to the scheduler and distinct by name in metrics.
- "Inconclusive", "parked", "churned" and "walked away" are `ended` states.

### 3. Rates are honest

- Every rate carries `hits` and `samples`.
- `value` is `null` when samples is 0.
- Every metric read made inside a policy is recorded on that policy's `decision` entry.

### 4. Flows are durable by replay

- Every `run`, `batch`, `halt`, `decide`, `move`, `update`, `remember` and `spawn` is a recorded entry with a sequence number.
- After a restart, the flow body is re-executed. Recorded results are returned without invoking anything again.
- Flow bodies must therefore be deterministic: they use `ctx.now()` and do no ambient I/O.
- A blocked attempt survives a restart and resumes at the same halt.

### 5. The flow's return value is the unit's resting state

| Return value | Effect |
|---|---|
| A `pending` state | Re-queues the unit. |
| A terminal state | Ends the unit. |
| An `idle` state | Parks the unit until a supplier update, trigger or operation moves it. |
| `ctx.until(rest, { at \| children, then })` | Parks the unit idle with a wake condition. |
| An `active`-mapped state | Fails the attempt. |

### 6. Flows speak the kinds they declare

- `H.flow(n).for(Bug, Feature)` types `ctx.unit.data` as `Bug | Feature`.
- `ctx.move` accepts only the states both kinds share.
- A lane accepts a flow only if the flow covers the lane's kind and the flow's states are among the kind's states.
- Per-lane differences are flow `params` supplied by the lane.

### 7. Moving a unit with a live attempt cancels the attempt first

This applies to moves from a supplier update, from a trigger's `act.move`, and from the `work.update` operation.

### 8. Supply

- A supplier emits `create` or `update`.
  - `create` is ignored if the key already exists.
  - `update` patches the store and may set a state.
- An update may re-open a terminal unit. Every terminal transition counts in metrics.
- The ledger keeps every unit's supplied snapshot, so a kind with no store still has data, state and telemetry.

### 9. Cost

- `maxUsdPerUnit` is cumulative across a unit's attempts.
- An invocation that would pass the ceiling halts the attempt with the kernel halt `cost-ceiling`.
- Daily budgets are scheduler-policy reads of `metrics.sum`.

### 10. Scheduler

- The harness has one schedule policy. It returns an ordered `start` list and an optional `preempt` list.
- The kernel starts units in that order while lane WIP and runner slots allow.
- Preempted attempts end `cancelled`, and their units return to their prior pending state.
- Blocked attempts release runner slots but still count toward lane WIP.
- Idle units count toward nothing.

### 11. Accounts and quota

- Account window state lives in the account's `QuotaBook`.
  - By default that is the ledger's quota section.
  - When accounts span harnesses, it is a shared book (`sqlite.quota(path)`).
- Shares belong to the pool, and therefore to one harness.

### 12. Memory

- The kernel owns the envelope: `id`, `created`, `when`, `status`.
- `candidate` items are never recalled until they are accepted.
- Recall always runs a recall policy over what the store's `search` returned.
- The flow narrows the recall scope for one invocation with `run(exec, input, { scope })`. This is how a section, a skill or a resource enters recall.
- Reads union across every library an agent `recalls`. Writes go to the one library it `records`.

### 13. Triggers

- The sources are `enters`, `streak`, `deadline` and `clock`.
- The effects are `create`, `move` and `remember`.
- Every firing is recorded.

### 14. Control API

- The API is made of operations, and clients are granted operations.
- The supervisor is `claude-code.supervisor`.
- A plain HTTP client is `http.control`.

### 15. Startup validation

`start()` fails in each of these cases:

- duplicate descriptor names;
- a lane/flow mismatch;
- an unknown state in a flow or trigger;
- an unregistered trigger lane;
- an agent no pool can serve;
- a command without argv or runner;
- a missing ledger;
- a batch call on a model that cannot batch.

Harnesses with no pools, agents or models are valid.

## Brief questions

- **Is `state` an entity?** No; it is cut. A lifecycle is a plain map.

- **Is `role` separate from `agent`?** Yes. Scenario 6 needs two agents of one role on different models in one flow.

- **Is `policy` one entity?** Yes, with six decision shapes. The scheduler is a policy plus `lane.wip`.
  - `pool` is kept as its own entity. Shares are runtime-editable configuration, and a policy may not change itself.

- **Is `journal` distinct from `lane`?** Yes, and it is renamed **library**.
  - Memory items have no lifecycle, no attempts and no scheduling.
  - Mapping them onto outcomes would be the lie that scenario 8 forbids.

- **Is `trigger` distinct from a flow step?** Yes.
  - Flows may only `spawn` their own children.
  - Triggers connect unrelated kinds, and time and patterns are their sources.

- **Is `supervisor` an entity?** No; it is cut. It is a client adapter.

- **Does a flow need `.input()`?** No. `.for(...kinds)` replaces it.

## Considered and cut

| Cut | Where it went |
|---|---|
| state | a plain map |
| scheduler | a policy |
| supervisor | a client |
| journal | library |
| step | invocation |
| observer as kernel entity | an adapter interface |
| resource entity | strings in scopes and leases |
| metric entity | `rate`/`rateBy` over tagged entries |
| hierarchy on kinds | `ctx.spawn` |
| `.key()` | supply |
| trigger `run` effect | removed |
| `timeout` | removed |
| `H.libraries()` | removed |
| separate tracker supplier/store | removed |

## What changed and why

Versus the brief and the seed weaknesses:

- Flows declare the kinds they speak (W1, W11).
- `spawn` plus `until(children)` replaces the slot-holding await (W2).
- Roles carry intents (W3).
- Triggers gain time and pattern sources (W5).
- Moves cancel live attempts, and the scheduler can preempt (W6).
- Deadlines are trigger sources, and the per-unit cost ceiling is a lane setting (W7).
- The `QuotaBook` can be shared (W8).
- Triggers can `remember`, with candidate status and curation (W9).
- Run, attempt and invocation are defined (W10).
- The read-union and write-one rule is stated for libraries (W12).
- `idle` and `ended` are added to the skeleton (W13).
- Clients name their transport (W15).
- Startup validation is specified (W16).
- Journal is renamed library (W17).

Changes made while writing the battery:

- **`RunOptions.scope`.**
  - Scenarios 1, 2 and 6 need one invocation's recall to be narrowed: the payments resource, the conversation category, the draft's section.
  - Before this change there was no way for the flow to tell recall what the current work touches.
  - The scope is merged into `RecallView.scope`.
- **`EntryFilter.status`.**
  - Approval rates (scenario 2) and editor-action rates (scenario 6) must count only `resolved` halt entries.
  - Without a status filter, the `raised` entries double the denominator.
- **`DataOf<K>` and `StateOf<K>` type helpers.**
  - A supplier `read` that maps many records to `Supply` values needs to name the supply type to keep state literals.
  - The alternative was `as const`, which the standard forbids.
- **Rule 5 states that returning an `idle` state parks the unit without a wake condition.**
  - Scenario 6 (a returned draft) and scenario 8 (a negotiation awaiting the vendor) wake on supplier updates, not on time.
- **The `.d.ts` files no longer contain Markdown code fences.** The fences made them uncompilable.
- **Scenario 7 defines its shared entities in one file.**
  - Scenario files may import only `harness-dsl`, so the "shared module" is a set of constants used by two harness descriptors in that file.
  - The design point is unchanged: descriptors are values, and two harnesses can hold the same one.

## Principles broken

- **12.** The five-outcome skeleton is replaced by seven: `idle` and `ended` are added.
  - **Why `idle`:** a tenancy or a negotiation must exist for years without holding capacity, and calling it `pending` would make it schedulable.
  - **Why `ended`:** experiments, parked topics and churn are terminal but neither success nor failure, and mapping them to `failed` or `cancelled` is a lie.
  - **What success rate means afterwards:** `succeeded / (succeeded + failed)`. `ended` and `cancelled` are reported beside it with their own counts.

=== END ===

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H, PendingView } from 'harness-dsl';
import * as claudeCode from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import * as anthropic from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import * as linear from 'harness-dsl/linear';
import * as folder from 'harness-dsl/folder';
import * as sqlite from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import * as jsonl from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import * as git from 'harness-dsl/git';
import * as shell from 'harness-dsl/shell';
import * as markdown from 'harness-dsl/markdown';

const ticket = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  description: z.string(),
  issueId: z.string().optional(),
});

const ticketLifecycle = H.lifecycle({
  todo: 'pending',
  building: 'active',
  auditing: 'active',
  done: 'succeeded',
  abandoned: 'failed',
  cancelled: 'cancelled',
});

const Bug = H.kind('Bug').data(ticket).states(ticketLifecycle, 'todo');
const Feature = H.kind('Feature').data(ticket).states(ticketLifecycle, 'todo');

const Epic = H.kind('Epic').data(ticket).states({
  todo: 'pending',
  planning: 'active',
  'in-progress': 'idle',
  integrating: 'pending',
  done: 'succeeded',
  failed: 'failed',
  cancelled: 'cancelled',
}, 'todo');

const Heartbeat = H.kind('ServiceHeartbeat').data(z.object({ service: z.string(), url: z.string() })).states({
  due: 'pending',
  probing: 'active',
  healthy: 'succeeded',
  down: 'failed',
}, 'due');

const Experience = H.memory('experience', 'fallible');
const Taste = H.memory('taste', 'owner');
const experience = H.library('experience', Experience, jsonl.memory('memory/experience.jsonl'));
const taste = H.library('taste', Taste, jsonl.memory('memory/taste.jsonl'));

const worktrees = git.worktree('worktrees', { repo: '.', slots: 4 });
const local = shell.local('local', { slots: 4 });

const projectChecks = H.command('project-checks').argv(() => ['npm', 'run', 'check']).on(worktrees);
const probeProduction = H.command('probe-production').argv(() => ['curl', '-fsS', 'https://app.example.com/health']).on(local);
const ping = H.command('ping-service')
  .input(z.object({ url: z.string() }))
  .argv(input => ['curl', '-fsS', '--max-time', '10', input.url])
  .on(local);

const builderRole = H.role('builder')
  .input(z.object({
    title: z.string(),
    description: z.string(),
    deficits: z.array(z.string()),
    answer: z.string().optional(),
  }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string(), question: z.string().optional() }))
  .prompt(input => [
    `Implement: ${input.title}`,
    input.description,
    input.deficits.length > 0 ? `Resolve these deficits:\n${input.deficits.join('\n')}` : '',
    input.answer ? `The owner decided: ${input.answer}` : '',
  ].join('\n\n'))
  .intents(['read', 'edit', 'execute', 'ask']);

const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string(), summary: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ deficits: z.array(z.string()) }))
  .prompt(input => `Audit the change for "${input.title}" against:\n${input.description}\n\nBuilder summary:\n${input.summary}\n\nList every deficit.`)
  .intents(['read', 'execute']);

const plannerRole = H.role('planner')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ features: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() })) }))
  .prompt(input => `Decompose the epic "${input.title}" into independently shippable features.\n\n${input.description}`)
  .intents(['read']);

const sonnet = claudeCode.model('claude-sonnet');
const opus = claudeCode.model('claude-opus');

const builderModel = H.policy.model('builder-model', choice => {
  const cheap = choice.metrics.successRate({ kind: choice.kind, model: sonnet.name, days: 14 });
  const tooFewSamples = cheap.samples < 20;
  const stillGood = cheap.value !== null && cheap.value >= 0.85;
  return tooFewSamples || stillGood ? sonnet : opus;
});

const builder = H.agent('builder', builderRole)
  .model(builderModel)
  .on(worktrees)
  .recalls(experience, taste)
  .guards(claudeCode.fileLeases(), claudeCode.stopCheck(projectChecks));

const auditor = H.agent('auditor', auditorRole)
  .model(opus)
  .on(worktrees)
  .recalls(experience)
  .records(experience);

const planner = H.agent('planner', plannerRole).model(opus).recalls(taste);

const subscriptionA = claudeCode.subscription('claude-a', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_A_TOKEN') });
const subscriptionB = claudeCode.subscription('claude-b', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_B_TOKEN') });
const subscriptionC = claudeCode.subscription('claude-c', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_C_TOKEN') });
const apiAccount = anthropic.account('anthropic-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') });

const soonestExpiringFirst = H.policy.account('soonest-expiring-first', choice => {
  const subscriptions = choice.accounts
    .filter(view => view.eligible && view.account.plan === 'subscription')
    .sort((a, b) => (a.windowEndsAt?.getTime() ?? Infinity) - (b.windowEndsAt?.getTime() ?? Infinity));
  const metered = choice.accounts.find(view => view.eligible && view.account.plan === 'metered');
  return subscriptions[0]?.account ?? metered?.account ?? null;
});

const claudePool = H.pool('claude', [
  { account: subscriptionA, share: 0.5 },
  { account: subscriptionB, share: 0.3 },
  { account: subscriptionC, share: 0.2 },
  { account: apiAccount, share: 1 },
], soonestExpiringFirst);

const touchedResources = (title: string): readonly string[] =>
  /payment/i.test(title) ? ['payments'] : [];

const ticketFlow = H.flow('build-and-audit')
  .for(Bug, Feature)
  .params(z.object({ rounds: z.number().int().positive() }))
  .does(async ctx => {
    const { title, description } = ctx.unit.data;
    const scope = { resources: touchedResources(title) };
    let deficits: readonly string[] = [];
    let answer: string | undefined;
    for (let round = 1; round <= ctx.params.rounds; round++) {
      await ctx.move('building');
      const built = await ctx.run(builder, { title, description, deficits: [...deficits], answer }, { scope });
      if (!built.ok) return 'abandoned';
      const question = built.value.question;
      if (question) {
        const decision = await ctx.halt({
          name: 'owner-decision',
          show: question,
          decision: z.object({ answer: z.string() }),
        });
        answer = decision.answer;
        continue;
      }
      await ctx.move('auditing');
      const audit = await ctx.run(auditor, { title, description, summary: built.value.summary }, { scope });
      if (!audit.ok) return 'abandoned';
      if (audit.value.deficits.length === 0) return 'done';
      deficits = audit.value.deficits;
    }
    return 'abandoned';
  });

const linearKey = H.env('LINEAR_API_KEY');
const ticketStatuses = {
  todo: 'Todo',
  building: 'In Progress',
  auditing: 'In Review',
  done: 'Done',
  abandoned: 'Canceled',
  cancelled: 'Canceled',
};

const linearBugs = linear.tracker(Bug, {
  apiKey: linearKey,
  team: 'ENG',
  label: 'bug',
  read: issue => ({ title: issue.title, description: issue.description, issueId: issue.id }),
  statuses: ticketStatuses,
});
const linearFeatures = linear.tracker(Feature, {
  apiKey: linearKey,
  team: 'ENG',
  label: 'feature',
  read: issue => ({ title: issue.title, description: issue.description, issueId: issue.id }),
  statuses: ticketStatuses,
});
const linearEpics = linear.tracker(Epic, {
  apiKey: linearKey,
  team: 'ENG',
  label: 'epic',
  read: issue => ({ title: issue.title, description: issue.description, issueId: issue.id }),
  statuses: {
    todo: 'Todo',
    planning: 'In Progress',
    'in-progress': 'In Progress',
    integrating: 'In Review',
    done: 'Done',
    failed: 'Canceled',
    cancelled: 'Canceled',
  },
});
const bugFiles = folder.files(Bug, {
  dir: 'bugs',
  read: file => ({ title: String(file.frontmatter.title ?? file.path), description: file.body }),
});

const bugLane = H.lane('bugs', Bug)
  .handler(ticketFlow, { rounds: 3 })
  .suppliers(linearBugs, bugFiles, H.operator)
  .store(linearBugs)
  .wip(2);

const featureLane = H.lane('features', Feature)
  .handler(ticketFlow, { rounds: 5 })
  .suppliers(linearFeatures, H.operator)
  .store(linearFeatures);

const epicFlow = H.flow('decompose-epic')
  .for(Epic)
  .does(async ctx => {
    if (ctx.unit.state === 'integrating') {
      const children = await ctx.children();
      return children.every(child => child.outcome === 'succeeded') ? 'done' : 'failed';
    }
    await ctx.move('planning');
    const plan = await ctx.run(planner, { title: ctx.unit.data.title, description: ctx.unit.data.description });
    if (!plan.ok) return 'failed';
    await ctx.spawn(featureLane, plan.value.features);
    return ctx.until('in-progress', { children: true, then: 'integrating' });
  });

const epicLane = H.lane('epics', Epic)
  .handler(epicFlow)
  .suppliers(linearEpics)
  .store(linearEpics)
  .wip(1);

const services = [
  { service: 'api', url: 'https://api.example.com/health' },
  { service: 'web', url: 'https://app.example.com/health' },
];

const heartbeatFlow = H.flow('heartbeat')
  .for(Heartbeat)
  .does(async ctx => {
    await ctx.move('probing');
    const probe = await ctx.run(ping, { url: ctx.unit.data.url });
    return probe.ok ? 'healthy' : 'down';
  });

const heartbeatLane = H.lane('heartbeats', Heartbeat)
  .handler(heartbeatFlow)
  .suppliers(H.schedule('every-five-minutes', Heartbeat, { every: { minutes: 5 } }, tick =>
    services.map(service => ({ create: service, key: `${service.service}-${tick.now.toISOString()}` }))));

const heartbeatFailureFilesBug = H.trigger('heartbeat-failure-files-bug', H.on.enters(Heartbeat, 'down'), (event, act) =>
  act.create(bugLane, {
    title: `Service ${event.unit.data.service} failed its heartbeat`,
    description: `Heartbeat ${event.unit.key} against ${event.unit.data.url} failed at ${event.at.toISOString()}.`,
  }));

const featureStarvationMs = 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
const rank = (unit: PendingView): number => {
  if (unit.lane === heartbeatLane.name) return 0;
  if (unit.lane === featureLane.name && unit.waitedMs > featureStarvationMs) return 1;
  if (unit.lane === bugLane.name) return 2;
  if (unit.lane === featureLane.name) return 3;
  return 4;
};

const scheduler = H.policy.schedule('heartbeats-bugs-features-epics', view => ({
  start: [...view.pending].sort((a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b) || b.waitedMs - a.waitedMs),
}));

export const harness = H.harness('coding-team')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('.harness/ledger.db'))
  .lanes(heartbeatLane, bugLane, featureLane, epicLane)

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H, PendingView, Metrics } from 'harness-dsl';
import * as anthropic from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import * as http from 'harness-dsl/http';
import * as sqlite from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import * as jsonl from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import * as shell from 'harness-dsl/shell';
import * as claudeCode from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import * as markdown from 'harness-dsl/markdown';

const conversation = z.object({
  conversationId: z.string(),
  customer: z.string(),
  message: z.string(),
  slaDueAt: z.string(),
  category: z.string().optional(),
});

const Conversation = H.kind('Conversation').data(conversation).states({
  new: 'pending',
  classifying: 'pending',
  drafting: 'active',
  'awaiting-approval': 'active',
  sent: 'succeeded',
  'closed-by-customer': 'ended',
  escalated: 'ended',
}, 'new');

const Escalation = H.kind('Escalation').data(z.object({
  conversationId: z.string(),
  reason: z.string(),
})).states({
  open: 'pending',
  handling: 'active',
  resolved: 'succeeded',
  abandoned: 'failed',
}, 'open');

const Taste = H.memory('taste', 'owner');
const Experience = H.memory('experience', 'fallible');
const taste = H.library('reply-taste', Taste, jsonl.memory('memory/taste.jsonl'));
const experience = H.library('support-experience', Experience, jsonl.memory('memory/experience.jsonl'));

const haiku = anthropic.model('claude-haiku');
const sonnet = anthropic.model('claude-sonnet');
const opus = anthropic.model('claude-opus');

const classifierRole = H.role('classifier')
  .input(z.object({ customer: z.string(), message: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ category: z.string() }))
  .prompt(input => `Classify this message from ${input.customer} into one support category:\n\n${input.message}`);

const drafterRole = H.role('drafter')
  .input(z.object({ customer: z.string(), message: z.string(), category: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ reply: z.string() }))
  .prompt(input => `Draft a reply to ${input.customer} about a ${input.category} issue:\n\n${input.message}`);

const draftApprovalRate = (metrics: Metrics) => metrics.rateBy({
  among: { entry: 'halt', halt: 'approve-reply', status: 'resolved' },
  count: { entry: 'halt', halt: 'approve-reply', status: 'resolved', decision: { approved: true } },
  by: { tag: 'draftModel' },
  days: 30,
});

const drafterModel = H.policy.model('drafter-model', choice => {
  const byModel = draftApprovalRate(choice.metrics);
  const challenger = byModel[opus.name];
  const incumbent = byModel[sonnet.name];
  if (!challenger || challenger.samples < 30 || !incumbent || incumbent.samples < 30) return sonnet;
  return (challenger.value ?? 0) > (incumbent.value ?? 0) + 0.05 ? opus : sonnet;
});

const classifier = H.agent('classifier', classifierRole).model(haiku);
const drafter = H.agent('drafter', drafterRole).model(drafterModel).recalls(taste, experience);

const safeCategory = H.policy.rule('safe-category', (input: { readonly category: string }, metrics: Metrics) => {
  const approvals = metrics.rate({
    among: { entry: 'halt', halt: 'approve-reply', status: 'resolved', tags: { category: input.category } },
    count: { entry: 'halt', halt: 'approve-reply', status: 'resolved', tags: { category: input.category }, decision: { approved: true } },
  });
  return approvals.samples >= 200 && approvals.hits === approvals.samples;
});

const local = shell.local('local', { slots: 8 });
const sendReply = H.command('send-reply')
  .input(z.object({ conversationId: z.string(), reply: z.string() }))
  .argv(input => ['helpdesk-cli', 'reply', input.conversationId, '--body', input.reply, '--token', H.env('HELPDESK_TOKEN')])
  .on(local);

const conversationFlow = H.flow('triage')
  .for(Conversation)
  .does(async ctx => {
    const { conversationId, customer, message } = ctx.unit.data;
    const classified = await ctx.run(classifier, { customer, message });
    if (!classified.ok) return 'escalated';
    const category = classified.value.category;
    await ctx.update({ category });
    await ctx.move('drafting');
    const draft = await ctx.run(drafter, { customer, message, category }, { scope: { skills: [category] } });
    if (!draft.ok) return 'escalated';
    ctx.tag({ category, draftModel: draft.model ?? 'unknown' });
    let reply = draft.value.reply;
    const safe = await ctx.decide(safeCategory, { category });
    if (!safe) {
      await ctx.move('awaiting-approval');
      const review = await ctx.halt({
        name: 'approve-reply',
        show: reply,
        decision: z.object({
          approved: z.boolean(),
          editedReply: z.string().optional(),
          tasteNote: z.string().optional(),
        }),
      });
      if (review.tasteNote) {
        await ctx.remember(taste, {
          text: review.tasteNote,
          status: 'candidate',
          when: { kinds: [Conversation.name], roles: [drafterRole.name] },
        });
      }
      if (!review.approved) return 'classifying';
      reply = review.editedReply ?? reply;
    }
    const sent = await ctx.run(sendReply, { conversationId, reply });
    return sent.ok ? 'sent' : 'escalated';
  });

const escalationFlow = H.flow('human-escalation')
  .for(Escalation)
  .does(async ctx => {
    await ctx.move('handling');
    const outcome = await ctx.halt({
      name: 'handle-escalation',
      show: `Conversation ${ctx.unit.data.conversationId}: ${ctx.unit.data.reason}`,
      decision: z.object({ resolved: z.boolean() }),
    });
    return outcome.resolved ? 'resolved' : 'abandoned';
  });

const helpdeskEvent = z.object({
  event: z.enum(['created', 'customer-replied', 'closed']),
  conversationId: z.string(),
  customer: z.string(),
  message: z.string(),
  slaDueAt: z.string(),
});

const helpdeskHeaders = { authorization: H.env('HELPDESK_TOKEN') };

const conversationLane = H.lane('conversations', Conversation)
  .handler(conversationFlow)
  .suppliers(
    http.webhook(Conversation, {
      path: '/hooks/helpdesk',
      secret: H.env('HELPDESK_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),
      body: helpdeskEvent,
      read: event => event.event === 'created'
        ? {
            create: { conversationId: event.conversationId, customer: event.customer, message: event.message, slaDueAt: event.slaDueAt },
            key: event.conversationId,
          }
        : event.event === 'customer-replied'
          ? { update: event.conversationId, patch: { message: event.message }, state: 'classifying' }
          : { update: event.conversationId, state: 'closed-by-customer' },
    }),
    http.poll(Conversation, {
      url: 'https://helpdesk.example.com/api/conversations?status=open',
      every: { minutes: 10 },
      headers: helpdeskHeaders,
      body: z.object({ conversations: z.array(helpdeskEvent) }),
      read: body => body.conversations.map(c => ({
        create: { conversationId: c.conversationId, customer: c.customer, message: c.message, slaDueAt: c.slaDueAt },
        key: c.conversationId,
      })),
    }),
  )
  .store(http.store(Conversation, {
    url: 'https://helpdesk.example.com/api/conversations',
    headers: helpdeskHeaders,
    stateField: 'harness_state',
  }))
  .maxUsdPerUnit(0.4);

const escalationLane = H.lane('escalations', Escalation).handler(escalationFlow);

const slaBreachEscalates = H.trigger(
  'sla-breach-escalates',
  H.on.deadline(Conversation, data => new Date(data.slaDueAt), ['new', 'classifying', 'drafting', 'awaiting-approval']),
  (event, act) => [
    act.create(escalationLane, { conversationId: event.unit.data.conversationId, reason: 'SLA breached' }, `sla-${event.unit.key}`),
    act.move('escalated'),
  ],
);

const timeToBreach = (unit: PendingView): number =>
  unit.is(Conversation) ? Date.parse(unit.data.slaDueAt) : -Infinity;

const scheduler = H.policy.schedule('time-to-breach', view => ({
  start: [...view.pending].sort((a, b) => timeToBreach(a) - timeToBreach(b)),
}));

const pool = H.pool('anthropic', [
  { account: anthropic.account('support-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') }), share: 1 },
], H.policy.account('first-eligible', choice => choice.accounts.find(view => view.eligible)?.account ?? null));

export const harness = H.harness('support-triage')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('.harness/ledger.db'))
  .lanes(conversationLane, escalationLane)
  .pools(pool)
  .triggers(slaBreachEscalates)
  .scheduler(scheduler)
  .clients(claudeCode.supervisor({
    grants: [H.ops.readWork, H.ops.resolveHalts, H.ops.readMemory, H.ops.writeMemory, H.ops.curateMemory, H.ops.readTelemetry],
  }))
  .observers(markdown.board('BOARD.md'), markdown.telemetry('TELEMETRY.md'));
